Content Introduction Text:
Attendee Verification Method 
 🌐 What Is This Functionality? The  Invitee Verification Method  is a setting on the  Event Settings  record that allows you to restrict who can register for your event. It ensures that only people you've explicitly invited can complete registration, based on how their identity is verified. 
 This is ideal for closed-door or high-security events where you need control over access but don?t want to require users to log in through Experience Cloud. 
 
 🔧 How Does It Work? You can find the  Invitee Verification Method  picklist on the Event Settings record. When set to  Attendee Email Match , it adds a verification step to the registration process when accessing the event through a public link: A user lands on the Event page. Before they can register, they're prompted to enter their email. The system checks to see if that email matches an existing Attendee record for the event. If matched, the user proceeds to register. If not matched, registration is blocked. This applies  only  to users accessing the event from a  public/generic event link . 
 If someone uses their  AttendeeLink  (the personalized link generated from the Attendee record), they skip the email prompt and go straight to registration. 📅 When Should I Use This? Use this setting when: You want to share one public registration link to a large invite list. You're using an external email tool (like Mailchimp or Pardot) to send invites and don't want to go over the 5,000 daily Salesforce Email limit for a mass Invitation email. You want to ensure that  only invited guests  can register. 📲 Example Use Case Marketing Team at FinServe Corp  wants to host a private investor webinar. They've uploaded 20,000 investor contacts into Salesforce as Attendee records. Instead of sending out 20,000 unique emails with as many individual Attendeelinks, they send one email campaign which includes their public Event Page URL (Or a link to the Event Group the Event is in). 
 With  Invitee Verification Method = Attendee Email Match , attendees are prompted to verify their email before seeing the registration form. Only those already in the system can continue. 
 This keeps the registration page secure, while making the invite process simple. 🔹 Key Considerations This setting is managed on the  Event Settings  record. Requires Attendee records to exist  before  invitees attempt to register. AttendeeLink bypasses email check and goes directly to the personalized form. 🎡 Pro Tips Customize the error message shown to unverified users by editing the site?s  Registration Page Error Text .

Content Introduction Text:
Invite Only Events via Visibility Controls 
 🌐 What Is This Functionality? Visibility Controls allow you to restrict who can register for an event by requiring a match between the Event or Event Item?s visibility control field value and the invited person (Attendee) record. This gives you a way to create invite-only access for events (or specific tickets)  without requiring login or Experience Cloud . 
 Instead, it?s based on values you set on the  Visibility Controls  field on both the Event or Event Item and the Attendee record. 🔧 How Does It Work? Here?s how to configure invite-only access using Visibility Controls: On the Event or Event Item, populate the  Visibility Controls  field with a value (e.g. "Members Only"). Pre-create Attendee records for invited guests with a Registration Status of "Invited". On each Attendee record, set their  Visibility Control  field to match the Event or Event Item. When the attendee accesses the Event or Item, Blackthorn checks for a matching value of the "Visibility Controls" field between the attendee and the Event or Item. If it matches, the Attendee can see and register. If not, access is denied. This method does  not require login  and works on public-facing pages. 📅 When Should I Use This? Use this method when: You want to restrict visibility to specific users without requiring login. You already have Attendee records created (or plan to create them in advance). You want more flexibility in controlling access to  specific tickets  (Event Items) within a single event. 📲 Example Use Case A university is hosting an event open to both students and alumni, but different ticket types should only be visible to one group or the other. The event organizer: Sets Visibility Controls = ?Student? on one Event Item and ?Alumni? on another. Pre-creates Attendee records for everyone they invited. Sets the Visibility Control field on each Attendee accordingly. Now, when invitees land on the event page, students only see the student ticket, alumni only see the alumni ticket. 
 This allows for  one public event page , but access to tickets is customized for the audience. Additionally, People visiting the Event page that were NOT pre-created Attendees will be able to see the Event page, but not any tickets to select from. 
 
 🔹 Key Considerations This setup  only works  if Attendee records are created  before  registration. Visibility Controls must match exactly (case-sensitive). Visibility Control fields exist on the following Objects, and you will need to make sure any custom Visibility Controls exist and match exactly: Event Event Item Session Event Item Session Attendee Contact If you don't set a value on the Event or Event Item, it's considered public. If an Attendee doesn?t have a matching value, they won?t be able to see or select the item. Attendees WILL need to use the AttendeeLink to access the event in order to see the tickets. 🎡 Pro Tips You can set the  Visibility Control  value on the  Contact  and use a simple Flow to copy it automatically to new Attendee records related to Contacts. Use Visibility Controls at the  Event Item  level to make only certain tickets invite-only, even if the event itself is public. You CAN use this functionality combined with Attendee Verification via email address to set up, authorized access only to the event and specific visibility to event items for your attendees.
Content Conclusion Text: Additional Resources Visibility Controls Learning Hub Content Visibility Controls Technical Documentation Screen Recording of a Flow to add Contact-level Visibility to related Attendee

Content Introduction Text:
Invite Only Events via Visibility Rules 
 🌐 What Is This Functionality? Visibility Rules  allow you to control who can see and register for events or ticket types based on advanced, dynamic logic. Unlike basic Visibility Controls, Visibility Rules let you reference fields on the Contact, User, or related objects to tailor access. 
 This approach is most effective in authenticated environments, such as  Experience Cloud sites  or  authenticated iFrames  embedded on your own website. It gives you invite-only behavior without requiring Attendee records to be created in advance. 🔧 How Does It Work? Here?s how to configure invite-only access using Visibility Rules: In the Event, Event Item, or Session, populate the  Advanced Visibility Rules  field with your criteria (e.g. Contact.Account.Name = "Board Members"). Publish the event in an  authenticated environment  (Experience Cloud or authenticated iFrame). When a logged-in user visits the page, Blackthorn evaluates the rule using the user's associated Contact record. If the rule evaluates as  true , the user sees and can register. If the rule evaluates as  false , the item (or event) is hidden from view. 📅 When Should I Use This? Use this method when: Your event is hosted inside a logged-in portal or authenticated web experience . You want to control visibility using criteria on the Contact or User record. You don?t want to pre-create Attendee records. You need flexibility beyond a single picklist value (e.g. role, account, or multi-field logic). 📲 Example Use Case A professional association uses an Experience Cloud portal to manage events for different membership levels. The team: Creates an event with several ticket types. Adds a Visibility Rule on the Event Item that says:  Contact.Membership_Tier__c = "Premium" . Only Premium-tier members who log into the portal see that ticket when viewing the event. This ensures each member sees only the ticket options meant for them?no manual attendee creation required. 🔹 Key Considerations Requires a  logged-in  user with an associated  Contact record . Rules must evaluate to  true or false . Cannot be used on unauthenticated public pages. Rules can be placed on: Event Event Item Session Event Item Session 🎡 Pro Tips Combine Visibility Rules with Event Group filtering to create full calendar segmentation. You can use more than one rule for different layers (e.g. Event has a rule, but each Event Item has its own rule as well). This is great for partner portals, member-only calendars, or gated internal events.

Content Introduction Text:
Invite Only Events 
 🌐 What Are Invite-Only Events? Invite-only events are events that aren?t open to just anyone. Whether it?s a VIP summit, an internal training, a donor appreciation dinner, or a members-only workshop, you sometimes need to make sure  only the right people can register. 
 Blackthorn offers multiple ways to make your events invite-only, depending on how tightly you want to control access and how your registration process is set up. 
 These invite-only options allow you to: Prompt invitees to verify their email before registering. Restrict visibility based on values set on their attendee or contact record. Use login-based rules for authenticated portals or embedded iFrames. Personalize access using individual registration links. Each method has different benefits and fits different types of event workflows. 🔧 How Does It Work? Here?s how to configure invite-only access using Visibility Rules: In the Event, Event Item, or Session, populate the  Advanced Visibility Rules  field with your criteria (e.g. Contact.Account.Name = "Board Members"). Publish the event in an  authenticated environment  (Experience Cloud or authenticated iFrame). When a logged-in user visits the page, Blackthorn evaluates the rule using the user's associated Contact record. If the rule evaluates as  true , the user sees and can register. If the rule evaluates as  false , the item (or event) is hidden from view. 📅 Common Use Cases You?re hosting a private leadership retreat and want to verify that only invitees can register, even from a public event link. You?re promoting a member-only event to the public, but only want members to see registration options. You want to manage tiered access to ticket types (e.g. Premium vs. Basic) for logged-in users. You?re sending out one universal invite link to a list of pre-approved partners and want to keep registration locked down. 🔹 Key Considerations Some methods  require pre-created Attendee records  (like email verification or visibility control). Some methods  require authentication  (like visibility rules for Experience Cloud or authenticated iFrames). Some methods are  great for public pages , others require gated access. Your choice depends on how you invite attendees, how secure you need registration to be, and whether you want to show or hide the event entirely. 🎡 Pro Tips Blackthorn also provides a few  Event Settings  that can enhance any invite-only setup: Disable "Not You" : Prevents users from clicking "Not You?" on an AttendeeLink. Useful if invites are forwarded and you don?t want someone else registering in place of the invitee. Disable Checkout As Someone Else : Hides the "Someone else" option in the contact info section during checkout. Helps lock registration to the intended recipient. Allow Edits to Attendee Fields : Allows or restricts invitees from updating name, email, or other fields that are pre-filled from their Attendee record via the AttendeeLink. These settings can be applied to any event using invite-only logic to further customize or restrict how attendees interact with their registration.

Content: Content Name: Displaying Table + Seat on Email Templates (Merge Tag Use Case)
Content Introduction Text:
Introduction In many event setups, attendees are assigned seats and tables. Often, customers want to display this seating information inside confirmation and reminder emails using merge tags (ex: ?Table A - Seat 12?). However, Blackthorn email templates can only merge fields that live directly on the Attendee record being emailed (ex: Attendee fields). If the seating information is stored only as a related record , it cannot be reliably pulled into email templates unless it is accessible through a Lookup field. This guide walks through how to store the seat relationship on the Attendee record so Blackthorn email templates can use it. 
 Why This Is Needed Right now: Seats are related to Attendees through a relationship But the Seat is not stored as a Lookup field on the Attendee That means the Attendee record does not have a direct reference to the Seat record Therefore, a formula field on the Attendee cannot reliably pull: Table Name Seat Number To solve this, we need to: Create a Seat Lookup field on the Attendee record Create a Flow that automatically populates that Seat Lookup when a Seat is assigned to an Attendee Create a formula field that combines Table + Seat into one text field Use that formula field as a merge tag in email templates 
 Pro-Tips Work in a Sandbox First: Always test in a Sandbox environment before production. Know Your Object Names: You may see ?Attendee? as a custom object name like conference360__Attendee__c. Flows Are Preferred: Salesforce Flow is the best modern tool for automation. Avoid Workflow Rules (deprecated). 
 Step 1: Create a Seat Lookup Field on the Attendee Object Goal Add a field to the Attendee record so it can store a direct link to the Seat record. Steps Go to Setup Click the gear icon (top right) Click Setup In the Setup search bar, type Object Manager Click Object Manager Find and select the Attendee object (This may be named something like Attendee or conference360__Attendee__c ) In the left menu, click Fields & Relationships Click New Choose Lookup Relationship Click Next Select the related object: Choose Seat Click Next Field Label: Label: Seat Field Name should auto-fill (example: Seat__c) Click Next Set Field-Level Security Make sure it?s visible for the profiles that need it (typically Admins) Click Next Add to Page Layouts Check the box to add it to all page layouts Click Save ? Result: The Attendee record now has a Seat Lookup field. 
 
 Step 2: Create a Flow to Automatically Populate the Seat Lookup Goal Whenever a Seat record is created or updated and linked to an Attendee, Salesforce should automatically update the Attendee record and populate the new Seat lookup field. Why This Matters Without automation, someone would have to manually populate the Seat field on the Attendee every time. Flow Requirements T rigger Object: Seat Trigger Type: Record is Created or Updated Condition: Seat has an Attendee assigned (Attendee is not blank) Action: Update the Attendee record?s Seat Lookup field with the current Seat record 
 Steps to Build the Flow Go to Setup Search for Flows Click Flows Click New Flow Select Record-Triggered Flow Click Create 
 Configure the Trigger Choose Object: Select Seat Trigger the Flow When: Select A record is created or updated Entry Conditions: Set condition: 
 Attendee (Seat?s attendee lookup field) Operator: Is Null Value: False This ensures the flow only runs when the Seat is tied to an Attendee. Optimize the Flow For: Select Actions and Related Records Click Done 
 Add the Update Records Element Click the + button under the Start node Select Update Records Label the element: Update Attendee Seat Lookup How to Find Records to Update: Choose Specify conditions to identify records, and set fields individually Object: Select Attendee Set Conditions (which Attendee should be updated?): Attendee Id equals the Seat record?s Attendee value Example: Field: Id Operator: Equals Value: $Record.Attendee__c Set Field Values (what should be updated?): Field to update: Seat__c (the new lookup field on Attendee) Value: $Record.Id Click Done 
 Save and Activate the Flow Click Save Flow Name: Populate Seat Lookup on Attendee Click Save Click Activate ? Result: Anytime a Seat is assigned to an Attendee, Salesforce automatically updates the Attendee and stores the Seat lookup. 
 Step 3: Create the ?Table & Seat? Formula Field on Attendee Goal Create a single text field on the Attendee that displays: Table Name - Seat Number Example: VIP Table A - Seat 12 
 Steps Go to Setup Go to Object Manager Select the Attendee object Click Fields & Relationships Click New Select Formula Click Next Field Label: Table & Seat Click Next Formula Return Type: Select Text Click Next 
 Paste This Formula 
 Seat__r.conference360__Table__r.conference360__Table_Name__c & " - Seat " & Seat__r.conference360__Seat_Number2__c 
 Click Check Syntax Click Next Set Field-Level Security Make visible to users who need it Click Next Add to Page Layout Check page layout boxes Click Save ? Result: The Attendee record now displays a combined Table + Seat field. 
 
 Step 4: Use the Table & Seat Field as a Merge Tag in Email Templates Goal Now that the data lives directly on the Attendee record, it can be pulled into email templates. Steps Go to your Blackthorn Email Template builder In the merge field selector, location and choose: Table & Seat Insert it into the email content Example: Your assigned seat is: {!Attendee.Table_Seat__c} ? Result: Confirmation and reminder emails will display seating information. 
 ? 
 Expected Outcome Once everything is complete: Seat records still relate to Attendees normally The Flow ensures the Attendee stores the Seat lookup automatically The formula field pulls the Seat?s Table Name and Seat Number Email templates can now display seating information using a merge tag FAQ?s Question : Why can?t we just pull the seat record directly in the email template? Answer: Salesforce merge tags generally only work for fields directly on the record. Related records don?t reliably merge unless accessed through a Lookup field relationship. 
 Question : Why do we need a Flow? Answer: A Flow ensures the Attendee Seat lookup is always automatically populated when a Seat record is created or updated. Without it, users would have to manually populate the lookup. 
 Question : What happens if an attendee?s seat changes? Answer: Since the flow triggers on Seat update, the Attendee lookup will update automatically as long as the seat record is updated correctly.

Content Introduction Text:
Salesforce Email Security Update (March 2026+) 
 Salesforce is increasing email security and will begin blocking emails sent from  unverified domains . This change may impact  Blackthorn Events and Payments notifications , since these rely on Salesforce email delivery. If your organization sends emails from a domain that is not verified in Salesforce, those emails may  fail to send . 
 Timeline Salesforce is rolling this out in stages: March 9  ? Enforcement begins for some orgs March 30  ? Sandbox org enforcement April 27  ? Existing production org enforcement To avoid interruptions and ensure your emails are sent, verify your domain   before these dates .
Content Conclusion Text:
What You Need to Do To ensure Salesforce can send emails successfully, verify your sending domain. 
 ??  Before You Begin ??  
 This setup typically requires access to  Salesforce settings and your organization?s DNS/domain provider . You may need to involve: A  Salesforce Administrator  (to configure DKIM, authorized domains, and email settings) The person or team who  manages your domain/DNS records  (such as IT or your website administrator) 
 Step 1 ? Create and Verify an Org-Wide Email Address Confirm that your sending email address is verified in Salesforce. Follow the instructions in this Learning Hub Content to set up your Organization-Wide email address. 
 
 Step 2 ? Configure DKIM Authentication DKIM confirms that Salesforce is authorized to send emails from your domain. Basic process: Go to Setup Search for DKIM Keys Click Create New Key Add your domain Add the generated CNAME record to your DNS provider (GoDaddy, Cloudflare, etc.) After DNS propagates, return to Salesforce and Activate the DKIM key 
 Step 3 ? Authorize Your Email Domain Salesforce also requires domain authorization. Go to Setup Search for Authorized Email Domains Click Add Enter your sending domain Add the provided TXT verification record to your DNS provider Return to Salesforce and click Verify 
 How to Confirm You're Done Your setup is complete when: DKIM key is Active Email domain is Verified Org-wide email addresses are Verified Once these are configured, Salesforce can safely send authenticated emails from your domain.

What Is the Event Builder? The Event Builder is your one stop shop for building out all your events in Blackthorn. With the Event Builder you can create your event, add tickets, sessions and attendees all in one place instead of clicking through 5+ Salesforce records. 
 Use Cases I am an event organizer and I need to create a last minute event and open it up for registration. By using the event builder, I can clone from a previous event and open up my new event for registration in less than 5 minutes! I am a system administrator and creating records in Salesforce is a breeze for me, but not for my event organizers. Instead of having them learn how to create new Salesforce records, I direct them to create their events, sessions, speakers, and event items from the builder's easy to use and intuitive UI! ?
Content Conclusion Text:
Sub-Features 
 🎙? Speakers One of the main benefits of using the event builder is that you get to create related records all in one go. Speakers are one of these related records. You can add and edit as many speaker records as you want, relate them to existing contacts, upload a profile photo straight from your computer and more! 
 🗓? Sessions You can also add sessions right from the builder, very similar to speakers, you can add and edit any existing sessions and even relate certain speakers to individual sessions. Add a banner, start and end time, price point, and description to your sessions all in one place. 
 🎟?Event Items Creating event items within the builder allows you to visually see the different types of event items your event has. You can easily see which event items are tickets, which are donations, and which are products. A big win over seeing plan records in Salesforce! 
 👥Attendee Loader Why do we put on events? To have people come to hem! Right from the builder you can bulk upload a list of invitees. No email is sent, but you?ll have everyones unique invitation link generated along with their attendee records so you can send those invites out whenever you are ready! 
 FAQ?s 
 Question: Can I add my own custom fields to the builder? Answer: Yes, you can do this if you have the permissions in Salesforce to do so by adjusting the field set (If you have the ability, you?ll see a click here hyperlink at the bottom of the builder). 
 Question: Can I leave the builder and pick up where I left off the next time I open it? Answer: Yes! But, don?t just leave the builder tab, click save and publish later to save the event and you?ll be able to click the builder button from the event record to pick up where you left off. 
 Question: Can I remove the ?Save and Publish? button from the builder? Answer: No, the UI inside the builder can?t be adjusted.  
 Additional Resources Blackthorn Documentation

Content Introduction Text:
What Are Event Tickets? Event Tickets are at the core of event registrations in Blackthorn. The reason? You can think of it this way, one ticket = one attendee in Salesforce. This allows for everybody in a group registration to get their own attendee records which allows for granular attendance tracking and pricing! 
 Use Cases I am an event organizer and I am setting up a student admissions event. I want to have two tickets, one for the student and one for the parents. I can create two event tickets so I can know who is who and capture relevant information. I am an event organizer and I need to limit how many people can register for a certain ticket for capacity reasons. I can use the tickets minimum and maximum quantity fields to only allow a certain number of tickets to be added to a cart during registration. ?
Content Conclusion Text:
Sub-Features 🗓? Sessions When it comes to opening up your sessions for registration, a key component is associated your sessions to a respective ticket. This allows you to control which sessions are seen as available depending on which ticket your registrants select, or you can just have all your sessions appear for all your tickets, the choice is yours! 
 🔒 Session Requirements You get to decide if one, some, or all of your tickets have Session related restrictions, including: "Required Sessions" that are added to the cart of the Attendee by default and cannot be removed, and "Require at least one Session" which requires an Attendee who chooses that Ticket to select at least one of the available sessions before they can check out. 
 📋 Custom Forms Sometimes it doesn't make sense to ask certain questions on certain ticket types. What if you have a parent ticket and a child ticket, it would be nice if you can only ask the parents questions and not have to repeat them for the child's ticket. Well good news is you can do just that by establishing a custom form on an individual ticket so you can ask the questions that make sense depending on the registrants choices. You can also remove/add any 'out of the box' questions per ticket. As an example, you can ask multiple questions to the parent, but only ask the name of the child and nothing else. You can control all of this by the attendee form on the ticket record. 
 FAQ's Question: Do I have to have a ticket related to my event? Answer: Yes and No. If you want to have your event open for registration, you have to have something for them to register for, so you would need at least one ticket. Although, you can save an event without a ticket and the event page will still load so it acts more like a digital flyer. 
 Question: Is there a limit to how many tickets I can have on one event? Answer: No! Although keep in mind the more choices you have the longer the scroll. 
 Additional Resources Blackthorn Documentation

Content Introduction Text:
What Are Blackthorn Products? You can think of Blackthorn Products as paid add-on's. Have your registrants pay for parking, buy a t-shirt, whatever you want. If you can type it you can sell it! It's important to note that Blackthorn doesn't do any inventory tracking, it simple adds the amount to the overall checkout transaction and a line item for the product on the related invoice. 
 Use Cases I am an event organizer and I want to allow my registrants to pay for merchandise in advance for convenience. I can use Blackthorn Products to expose my merch with their associated prices so my registrants can add them to their cart along with their tickets. I am in charge of finance and I need to see clearly how much money went to the admission costs and how much went towards merchandise sales. I can pull a report to see invoices, line items, and transactions to accomplish this. ?
Content Conclusion Text:
Sub-Features 👥Attendee Records What if someone does purchase a product during registration, how will you know? In addition to the line item on the invoice, you'll see a checkbox on the attendee record marked as true. The checkbox is called 'Purchased Product'. 
 💰 Invoices & Line Items Associated to every attendee record will be an invoice where you can see what they purchased. From here you can see each product (along with tickets and donations) broken out into their own respective line items. 
 FAQ?s 
 Question: Can I have multiple products available durning registration? Answer: Yes! There is not limit to how many products you can make available. 
 Question: Can I put a certain amount of availability on a product so I don't oversell? Answer: Yes, you can establish how much you have available and once a certain number of people have purchased it, it'll show as sold out.

Content Introduction Text:
What Are Donations at Checkout? Use Blackthorn's Donation Event Items to easily add charity donations to your event registration. This tool lets you set up and manage donation options, giving attendees the chance to donate to their chosen cause while signing up for the event. They can pick a set donation amount or enter their own. This feature makes supporting charities simple during event registration and improves the overall charitable aspect of your event. 
 Use Cases A university or a non-profit organization uses Blackthorn's Donation Event Items for their fundraisers. Both allow attendees to give preset or custom donations. Each donation is tracked as a separate Salesforce opportunity, simplifying the process and providing insights into fundraising effectiveness for future event planning and donor engagement.
Content Conclusion Text:
Sub-Features 
 ? Opportunities on Checkout Blackthorn's Donation Event Items now include the "Opportunities on Checkout" feature to improve your event's fundraising. This addition integrates Salesforce opportunities into event registrations. Organizers can create a single opportunity for the entire event to track overall fundraising, and also record individual opportunities for each donation made during checkout. This ensures all donations, whether preset amounts or custom figures, are accurately tracked. This feature links event registrations and donations to Salesforce, giving a detailed view of your event's fundraising success. 
 FAQ?s 
 Question: Can I have multiple donations available? Answer: Yes, you can have multiple donations related to one event and the registrant can add as many as they'd like during one registration flow. 
 Question: Does each donation create it's own opportunity in Salesforce? Answer: Yes! It's a handy way to track each donation, each opportunity will all be associated to the invoice for the registration if you have opportunities for donations enabled on the associated event settings. 
 Question: Are donations charged in separate transactions? Answer: No, even though the donation will have it's own line item and opportunity (if enabled), the overall checkout is charged as one transaction unless you are using our split transaction functionality. 
 Additional Resources Blackthorn Documentation for Opportunities on Checkout Blackthorn Documentation on Donations Blackthorn Documentation on Event Items

Content Introduction Text:
What Are Sessions? As you create your events you may have a need to have smaller break-out gatherings within the event itself. Sessions can be added to your event for attendees to join in addition to your larger event. They aren?t required but you can add as many as you like, and they can be either in-person or virtual as well as free or paid. 
 Use Cases I am an event organizer and I have multiple sessions to choose from. Instead of just showing all of my sessions at once during registration, I can have certain sessions appear for certain ticket types to give a more refined checkout experience. As an event organizer, I want to let people know that certain speakers will be at certain sessions. I can easily relate one or more speakers to an individual session from the wizard and builder.
Content Conclusion Text:

📝 Forms & Custom Questions Blackthorn?s  Forms  feature allows you to go beyond the basics of name and email collection. With Forms, you can create custom questions that appear at different stages of registration, on specific tickets, or even tied to sessions. This flexibility ensures you gather the right information at the right time?without overwhelming your attendees. 🎯 Where Questions Can Appear Blackthorn supports  five locations  where forms and questions can be displayed: 
 Stage Scope When They Show Notes Standard Event-Item (Attendee Form) Ticket-level During checkout Built-in standard fields (Name, Email, Phone, etc.) configured on the Event Item record. Pre-Registration Form (Custom Questions) Event-level or Ticket-level During checkout Attendees cannot complete registration until these are answered. Assign at the event for all tickets, or at a ticket for item-specific questions. Session Forms Session-level When attendee selects a specific session Add questions tied directly to sessions (e.g., ?Meal preference for this workshop??). Newer feature. Post-Registration Form AttendeeLink After registration Questions appear when attendees open their AttendeeLink (e.g., collect travel info closer to event date). Post-Event Survey Event / Item / Attendee After the event Gather feedback through attendee-specific survey links, typically sent via email. 
 
 
 ? How It Works Layering : Event-level questions apply to everyone, ticket-level forms only apply to that ticket type, and session forms only appear if the session is chosen. Conditional Logic : Show or hide questions based on prior answers (e.g., ?If Other is selected, show text field for details?). Data Storage : All answers are stored in  Form Submission Answer  records and linked to the Attendee. Field Mapping : Responses can map back to Salesforce records (Attendee, Contact, Lead, or Account) for reporting and automation.

Watch Limits : Avoid overusing long text fields (Text 30k) to prevent Salesforce payload errors. Answering Form Questions Blackthorn Events allows for customizable registration forms where attendees can answer specific questions: Conditional Questions : These questions change based on previous answers. File Uploads : Attendees can upload files as part of their registration, which are then stored in Salesforce and associated with their records. What are Scheduled Jobs Scheduled jobs in Blackthorn Events are essential for maintaining the efficiency and accuracy of event management tasks. These jobs automate various processes, ensuring that data is updated, attendees are managed, and events run smoothly. Here?s a brief overview of why they are important and how to manage them. Why Scheduled Jobs Are Important Scheduled jobs automate critical tasks such as updating attendee statuses, processing form submissions, and refreshing event caches. This automation helps reduce manual work, minimizes errors, and ensures timely updates, which are crucial for accurate event management and reporting. Key Scheduled Jobs Process No-Show Attendees Runs: Nightly at 11:00 pm Function: Updates an attendee's status to "No-Show" if the event has ended and the status is not "Attended". 
 Attendee Parent Rollup Runs: Nightly at 2:00 am Function: Updates the "Events Attended" field on the attendee's parent record based on their attendance status. 
 Form Submission Processing Runs: Every hour and every five minutes Function: Processes form submissions and links answers to relevant Salesforce records. 
 Geocode Service Runs: Nightly at 10:00 pm Function: Updates geocode information for event venues based on the provided address. 
 Webinar Account Refresh Runs: Daily at 2:00 am Function: Ensures webinar account tokens do not expire. 
 Recurring Event Generate Runs: Nightly at 3:00 am Function: Updates and creates recurring events based on specified recurrence methods. 
 Status Update Runs: Nightly at 1:00 am Function: Updates event statuses to "Completed" and unpublishes them if the event has ended. 
 Batch Event Registration Submission Runs: Every minute Function: Processes event registration submissions in batches. 
 Revenue Rollups Runs: When an event status is set to "Ended" Function: Rolls up financial summaries for event items and events. How to Manage Scheduled Jobs Schedule Jobs: Navigate to the Blackthorn | Events Admin tab. Click the Scheduled Jobs tab. Click Schedule Recommended Event Jobs to schedule all recommended jobs. 
 Change Scheduled Job User: Ensure the user has Admin access. Follow the steps to delete current jobs and reschedule them under the new user. Go to the Blackthorn | Events Admin tab.  Click the Scheduled Jobs tab.  Click  Schedule Recommended Event Jobs . This will delete/UNschedule the existing jobs and create a new Scheduled Job. 
 
 View and Manage Jobs: Go to Setup Menu  > Jobs > Scheduled Jobs. All of the names start with Blackthorn | Events Perform actions like editing, archiving, or unscheduling based on the job status.
Content Conclusion Text:
FAQ Q: Why do I see multiple jobs with the same name or very similar names? A: When we update the app, sometimes the jobs need to be updated to include new Features, Objects, and Fields; So we update the job or Job name to include the required new items. Occasionally, the new job added or updated results in what LOOKS like a duplicate job. If you're concerned, use the "Schedule Recommended Jobs" button from the Events Admin tab to make sure you're up to date!

Vanity Domain (Customized Events Domain) Blackthorn Events allows you to use a custom domain for your event pages, providing a seamless and branded experience for your attendees. Setting up a vanity domain requires coordination between your DNS settings and Blackthorn's configuration. 
 Key Steps to Configure a Vanity Domain Step 1- DNS Configuration Enter your vanity domain in the Blackthorn | Events Admin tab under Settings. You will want to make sure your domain is something like: Events.YOURDOMAIN.com Submit this information to Blackthorn Support at least 48 hours before you need to use the custom domain . Blackthorn will provide you with the necessary CNAME and TXT endpoints to update your DNS records. This will look something like this: Here are the DNS records. Please let us know when this is complete and we will then proceed with the final step. Thank you! 
 Certificate validation TXT name _acme-challenge. YOUR.NEWDOMAIN.com Certificate validation TXT value 6cod6NKGOi2AF3jHNi4fOcijNatrKzO768QQvAUDWAQ 
 Hostname pre-validation TXT name _cf-custom-hostname.events. YOUR.NEWDOMAIN.com Hostname pre-validation TXT value b76dal42-edqb-63eb-b6ad-872d3r2bag3b 
 We need to complete this step ahead of time because when you update the "Domain" field, it redirects all of your Event URLs to that domain and temporarily breaks them until the setup is complete. 
 Step 2- Confirm Updates You'll give the information you received from Support to the person managing your domain and have them update the DNS records. Let us know when they've completed that task so we can get you the SSL Cert, and confirm the feature is enabled for your org! The next step is to create the CNAME record for (YOURDOMAIN.COM) and point it to events.blackthorn.io. Again, your Domain Manager should be able to handle that for you! 
 Step 3- Update Salesforce Settings: Remote Site Settings: Click the  Gear  icon located in the upper right-hand corner. Click  Setup . Enter "Remote Site Settings" in the Quickfind box. Click Events_Domain Click  Edit . Change the 'Remote Site URL' from "https://events.blackthorn.io" to "https://events.YourDomainName.com" Update Platform Domain: from the setup menu, type "Custom Settings" in the search bar at the top. Find "Event Settings" and click "Manage" Next to it. Click "Edit" Update the Platform Domain field to match the new Remote Site URL.

Content: Content Name: Add 'From Addresses' for Blackthorn's Email Components
Content Introduction Text:
Setting Up Organization-Wide Addresses in Salesforce Adding organization-wide email addresses in Salesforce is essential for ensuring that Blackthorn's email components can reference the correct 'From Address' when sending communications. This guide will walk Salesforce Administrators through the steps to add these addresses and explain to Event Organizers the benefits of having organization-wide addresses configured. 
 Why Beneficial? Needed for Blackthorn Emails: Blackthorn's email components can only pull from organization-wide addresses so it's crucial you have at least one available for use if you plan on using Blackthorn's email components. Consistency: Using organization-wide addresses ensures that all outgoing emails have a consistent 'From Address', enhancing brand recognition and trust. Management: Centralized management of email addresses makes it easier to update and maintain contact details. Compliance: Helps in adhering to organizational policies and compliance requirements for communication. Steps for Salesforce Administrators: Navigate to Organization-Wide Addresses: Go to Setup. In the Quick Find box, type "Organization-Wide Addresses". Select "Organization-Wide Addresses" under Email. Add a New Email Address: Click the "Add" button to create a new organization-wide email address. Fill in the necessary details: Display Name: The name that recipients will see. Allow All Profiles to Use this From Address: Check this box if you want all profiles to be able to use this email address. Click "Save". Email Address: The email address that will be used as the 'From Address'. Verify the Email Address: Salesforce will send a verification email to the specified email address. Access the email account and click on the verification link provided in the email. Once verified, the email address will be available for use in Salesforce. Assign Email Address to Profiles: If you did not select "Allow All Profiles to Use this From Address", you will need to assign the email address to specific profiles. Click on "Organization-Wide Addresses" again. Click on the name of the email address you added. Under "Available Profiles", select the profiles that should use this email address and click "Add". Explanation for Event Organizers: Consistency in Communication: Using organization-wide addresses ensures that all emails sent from Salesforce, whether they are event invitations, reminders, or follow-ups, come from a consistent and recognizable email address. This helps build trust with recipients and maintains a professional appearance. Efficiency and Management: With predefined organization-wide addresses, you do not need to manually enter or remember different email addresses for various communications. This reduces the chance of errors and simplifies the process of sending out emails. Compliance and Control: Organization-wide addresses ensure that all communications adhere to the company?s policies. It centralizes control over the email addresses used, ensuring that all outgoing communications are compliant with legal and organizational standards. Enhanced Deliverability: Emails sent from a verified and consistent address are less likely to be marked as spam. This increases the likelihood that your event communications will reach your intended audience.
Content Conclusion Text:
By setting up organization-wide email addresses, Salesforce Administrators ensure that Blackthorn's email components can reference the correct 'From Address', providing consistency, efficiency, and compliance benefits. Event Organizers benefit from streamlined communication processes and improved deliverability, ensuring that their event-related emails are professional and trustworthy. 
 FAQ's Question: Why do we need organization-wide email addresses in Salesforce? Answer: Organization-wide email addresses provide a consistent 'From Address' for all outgoing emails, enhancing professionalism, trust, and compliance with organizational policies.

What Are UTM Parameters? What in the world is a UTM Parameter?! This stands for Urchin Tracking Module. Still confused? To put it simply, for Blackthorn UTM Parameters allow you to track how Attendees registering for your events came to find your event in the first place. Or anything else you want to track associated with an Attendee registering.  
 Use Cases For example you?re promoting your upcoming event on Instagram, through Email Marketing, and on your website. They can also be used in a Sales context as you can have a individual link for each Sales rep and easily track how may registrations they influence. Now that you know what UTM Parameters are you can set them up for your events to allow for easy reporting on which marketing channels are the most effective to focus on more in the future!  
 Still not sure on what UTM parameters are or how to use them? Ask someone from your Sales or Marketing team as this would be a feature they are interested in. We have found that this is a very underrated feature but when understood on how it can help with organization?s use cases it becomes one of the most important features for return on investment tracking. 
 You'll need to add "?[Parameter Form Question}=[value you want to track]" to the end of your event page URL, the bracketed text will need to be replaced with your Parameter Form Element question and the tracking value. 
 ? You can also combine multiple UTM's into one URL using "&". This can be used to track email registrations as the source while still tracking which team member on your team is sending the email for example!

Content: Content Name: Setting Up Stripe Checkout with Blackthorn Events
Content Introduction Text:
How to Setup Stripe Checkout with Blackthorn Events Integrating Stripe Checkout with Blackthorn allows you to seamlessly process payments for your events, ensuring a smooth and secure transaction experience for your attendees. Stripe Checkout is a pre-built, hosted payment page optimized for conversion, making it an excellent choice for event organizers who want to offer a reliable and user-friendly payment solution. 
 Why Use Stripe Checkout? Secure Payments : Stripe ensures high-level security and compliance for all transactions. User-Friendly : A streamlined, easy-to-navigate payment interface enhances the attendee experience. Modern Payment Methods : Allows the use of Apple Pay and Google Pay for a faster checkout experience. 
 Steps to Setup Stripe Checkout: Set Up a Stripe Account : If you don't already have a Stripe account, sign up at Stripe's website . Complete the necessary verification and business information steps. Request Stripe Checkout Activation : Contact Blackthorn's onboarding or support team to activate Stripe Checkout for your account. Link Stripe to Blackthorn (if you haven't done so already) : In Salesforce, navigate to the Blackthorn Events app. Go to "Payment Gateways" and click on "New" to add a new payment gateway. Select "Stripe" as the provider. Click 'Connect to Gateway' and log into your Stripe account. Note: If you want to test stripe checkout, this also works with test stripe accounts, just mark your payment gateway as 'Test' and then click the 'Connect to Gateway' button. This will give you the ability to skip the login process. Configure Event Settings : Navigate to Setup. Use the Object Manager to find the Event Settings object. Click Fields & Relationships on the Event Settings object. Search for and select 'Enabled Payment Methods'. Go to the Values section and click New. Add "Stripe Checkout" to the text box. Click Save. Navigate to the Event Settings object you want to use for Stripe Checkout transactions. Edit the Enabled Payment Method field to include "Stripe Checkout". Note : If using Stripe Checkout, do not enable other payment methods except Pay Later. Configure the Payment Gateway : Navigate to the Payment Gateway object in Setup. Click Page Layouts. Click Payment Gateway Layout. Add the Accepted Checkout Payment Methods field to the page layout. Navigate to the Stripe Payment Gateway that will be used for Stripe Checkout. Edit the Accepted Checkout Payment Methods field to include the payment methods to be used for Stripe Checkout. If you are just using apple or google pay, then just move over the 'Card' option as these mobile options will automatically appear if you are testing on a device that supports these methods. Add Permissions to Access Encrypted Data : Create a new permission set in Setup. Name it "Access Encrypted Data". Navigate to System Permissions. Click Edit. Check the View Encrypted Data checkbox. Save the permission set. Navigate to the user record in Setup for the person who authenticated the Events app. Add the permission set you just created to that individual's user record. Setup Webhooks : If you haven't already set up webhooks in your org, you'll want to do this. Stripe Checkout utilizes data brought into the org via webhooks. Related records like Payment Method and Payment Gateway Customer are attached to the transaction after the webhooks process. Test Setup : Create a test event and simulate a payment to ensure everything is working correctly. Verify that the payments are processed through Stripe and that the transactions appear in both your Stripe and Salesforce records. Go Live : Once testing is complete and everything is functioning correctly, set your events to live. Monitor the transactions and ensure that the payment processing runs smoothly during the event registration period.
Content Conclusion Text:
FAQ's Question: How do I handle refunds through Stripe Checkout?  Answer: Refunds work the same way as regular checkouts, you can go to the related invoice and hit the refund button. 
 Question: Is Stripe Checkout available in all countries?  Answer: Stripe Checkout is available in many countries, but availability may vary. Check Stripe's supported countries list on their website. 
 Question: Why should I use Stripe Checkout with Blackthorn Events?  Answer: One of the most common reasons to use Stripe Checkout with Blackthorn Events is to enable modern payment methods like Apple Pay and Google Pay, providing a faster and more convenient checkout experience for attendees. 
 Additional Resources Stripe Checkout Documentation

Content Introduction Text:
Introduction The Event Registration Submission (ERS) record in Blackthorn is designed to streamline and secure the event registration process by capturing all registration data in a single object before processing it into Salesforce. This approach minimizes errors and improves the attendee experience by preventing direct Salesforce interaction during registration.? 
 Purpose of ERS Records ERS records serve as an intermediary to collect and validate registration data in a JSON format. This ensures that if there are any issues, they are handled internally without affecting the attendee?s registration experience. The system then processes the collected data, creating the necessary Salesforce records such as Attendees, Invoices, and Contacts or Leads. 
 Benefits for Event Organizers Error Handling : Any errors during registration are captured and can be addressed without the attendee seeing any error messages. Data Integrity : Ensures all data is correctly processed into Salesforce without interruptions from custom processes or validations. Simplified Troubleshooting : Provides clear error messages and a straightforward method to reprocess failed submissions. 
 Pro Tips Automated Notifications : Use the built-in workflow rule to receive notifications when an ERS fails, allowing you to quickly address issues. JSON Data Review : Review the JSON data in ERS records to understand and debug any registration issues. Reprocessing Failures : Change the status from "Failed" to "Processed" and check the process checkbox to reprocess an ERS record. ?
Content Conclusion Text:
The ERS object in Blackthorn Events significantly enhances the registration process by capturing and processing data efficiently, reducing errors, and improving the overall attendee experience. By understanding how to navigate and utilize ERS records, event organizers can ensure smooth and error-free event registrations. 
 FAQ Question: How do I navigate to the Event Registration Submission object? Answer: Go to the App Launcher, type in "Events Admin," and select the "Event Registration Submission" tab. Question: What do I do if an ERS fails? Answer: Review the error message provided in the ERS record, address the issue in your form or process, and then reprocess the ERS by changing its status and checking the process checkbox. If all else fails, send the ERS record over to Blackthorn Support for assistance!

Content: Content Name: What Permission Sets Do My Users Need?
Content Introduction Text:
What Permission Sets Do My Users Need? 
 When assigning permission sets to your users for Events and Payments, it's crucial to understand the specific needs and roles of each user. Below, we'll outline the various permission sets available, provide use cases and examples, and explain how licensing impacts permissions. 
 Events Permission Sets Blackthorn | Events Admin Use Case:  For users managing event configurations, settings, and overall event administration. Example:  An Event Manager responsible for creating and managing events, tracking registrations, and overseeing event logistics. This permission set grants full access to the Events Admin tab and all objects, including custom objects and specific Payments features like Relationship Settings and Codes. Salesforce Admin:  Setting up the Blackthorn implementation. Event Manager:  Overseeing the creation and management of multiple events. Operations Director:  Needing full access to all event-related data and configurations to ensure seamless execution of events. 
 Blackthorn | Events Organizer Use Case:  For users creating and managing events, coordinating event logistics and operations. Example:  An Event Coordinator handling event setup, attendee management, and on-the-day logistics. This permission set includes View/Modify/Delete access to custom objects and Read permissions for Payment Gateways. Event Coordinator: Handling event setup, attendee management, and day-of logistics. Logistics Specialist: Managing vendor coordination and event setup details. Volunteer Manager: Assigning and overseeing volunteer tasks during events. 
 Blackthorn | Events Lite User Use Case:  For users needing limited access to manage attendees. Example:  Event staff checking in attendees and managing attendee groups. This permission set allows Create/Read/Edit access to attendee-related objects and Read-only access to most Events objects. Event Staff:  Checking in attendees and managing attendee groups. Registration Desk Personnel:  Handling on-site attendee registrations and modifications. Customer Service Representative:  Assisting with attendee inquiries and updates. 
 Blackthorn | Events Limited Access (Minimum permission needed for Check-in app) Use Case:  For users requiring minimal access to specific event data. Example:  Temporary staff needing to view and update event and attendee records without broader access. This set provides Create/Read/Update permissions for Event and Attendee objects only. Temporary Staff:  Viewing and updating event and attendee records without broader access. Data Entry Clerk:  Updating attendee information as needed. Support Staff:  Assisting with basic event data management tasks. 
 Blackthorn | Events Community/Platform User Use Case:  For community or platform users interacting with event data. Example:  Community members needing to engage with event records. This set offers Create/Read/Update permissions for all Event objects but restricts access to specific fields like Leads and Opportunities. Community Member:  Engaging with and registering for events. External Partner:  Collaborating on event details without accessing sensitive data. 
 Blackthorn | Events Read Only Use Case:  For users who need to review event data without making changes. Example:  Executives or auditors needing to monitor event performance and statistics. This set provides Read-Only access to Events objects. Executive:  Monitoring event performance and statistics. Auditor:  Reviewing event-related data for compliance purposes. Board Member:  Keeping informed on event activities and outcomes. Payments Permission Sets Blackthorn | Payments Admin Use Case:  For users managing payment configurations, transactions, and financial reporting. Example:  Finance Managers responsible for overseeing payment processing, issuing refunds, and generating financial reports. This set grants full access to all payment-related objects and settings. Finance Manager:  Overseeing payment processing, issuing refunds, and generating financial reports. System Administrator:  Setting up and configuring payment gateways and settings. Payments Specialist:  Managing all aspects of payment data and configurations. 
 Blackthorn | Payments User Use Case:  For users who need to process payments but do not require full administrative access. Example:  Sales representatives processing sales transactions and setting up payment plans for customers. This set provides read access to Payment Gateway and Webhook Event objects, and read/create access to the Blackthorn Log object. Sales Representative:  Processing customer payments and setting up payment plans. Customer Service Agent:  Handling payment inquiries and processing refunds. Account Manager:  Managing client payment transactions and follow-ups. 
 Blackthorn | Payments Manager Use Case:  For managers overseeing payment operations without needing full admin privileges. Example:  A Payments Operations Manager who supervises payment processing and handles escalated issues. This set provides delete access to custom objects except for Payment Gateway and Webhook Event objects. Payments Operations Manager:  Supervising payment processing and handling escalated issues. Financial Analyst:  Reviewing and managing payment data and reports. Department Head:  Overseeing department-specific payment activities and data. 
 Blackthorn | Payments Community/Platform User Use Case:  For community or platform users interacting with payment data. Example:  Community members needing to view payment records. This set is similar to the Payments User permission set but does not include any Assigned Apps, making it suitable for community users. Community Member:  Viewing payment records and transaction history. 
 Blackthorn | Payments Site Guest User Use Case:  For guest users needing to create webhook events. Example:  External users triggering webhook events from Stripe. This set includes permissions necessary for creating Webhook Events. External User:  Triggering webhook events from Stripe. Integration Specialist:  Setting up and testing webhook integrations. API Developer:  Managing webhook events and ensuring proper integration. Pro Tips Site License:  If your organization has a site license, you can assign as many of each permission set as needed without additional costs. User-Based License:  If you have a user-based license, ensure that each user with a permission set also has a license for the corresponding app. This prevents access issues and ensures compliance with licensing terms. Important Note for Events Admins Any user with the  Events Admin  permission set, especially authorized users, should also have the  Payments License and Payments Admin permission set. This ensures they have the necessary access to manage payment-related tasks associated with events, such as processing registrations, handling refunds, and generating financial reports.
Content Conclusion Text:
Properly assigning permission sets based on user roles and ensuring compliance with licensing terms will streamline your operations and enhance security. For detailed steps and additional information, refer to the Blackthorn documentation.

Content: Content Name: Mapping Salesforce Metadata to Stripe in Blackthorn
Content Introduction Text:
Introduction Mapping Salesforce metadata to Stripe is a powerful feature in Blackthorn that allows you to seamlessly transfer custom data from Salesforce to Stripe transactions. This ensures that all relevant information is carried over, providing a complete view of transactions for reporting, analytics, and customer insights. 
 What is Salesforce to Stripe Metadata Mapping? Salesforce to Stripe metadata mapping involves configuring custom fields in Salesforce to be included as metadata in Stripe. Metadata in Stripe is used to store additional information about the transaction that can be used for various purposes such as reporting, searching, and custom business logic. 
 Why Use Salesforce to Stripe Metadata Mapping? Enhanced Data Transfer : Ensures all relevant information is included in Stripe transactions. Custom Reporting : Facilitates advanced reporting and analytics by including custom fields. Improved Customer Insights : Provides a more comprehensive view of the transaction and customer behavior. ? How to Map Salesforce Metadata to Stripe Navigate to Custom Metadata Types : In Salesforce, go to Custom Metadata Types. Select Stripe Metadata Mappings : Under the label's section, select "Stripe Metadata Mapping". Create New Mapping : Click "Manage Stripe Metadata Mappings" to create a new metadata mapping. NOTE: If you want to see the information in Stripe on the Transaction, then you need to make sure to create a field on the Blackthorn "Transaction" Object that houses that information. Only metadata mappings from the Transaction will map into Stripe on the Stripe Transaction. Define Mapping Details : Salesforce Field : Select the Salesforce field that you want to map. Stripe Key : Enter the key name for the metadata in Stripe. Save the Mapping : Save your changes to apply the mapping. ? Example Scenario Suppose you want to include a custom field from Salesforce, such as "Customer Loyalty Level," in your Stripe transactions. By creating a metadata mapping for this field, every transaction processed through Stripe will include the customer's loyalty level, allowing for better segmentation and targeted marketing. 
 Detailed Walkthrough Setting Up the Page Layout : Navigate to "Custom Metadata Types" and search for "Stripe Metadata Mapping". Click on the label and ensure the fields (like Metadata Key) are visible on the layout by editing the page layout if necessary. Creating a New Mapping : Go to "Manage Stripe Metadata Mappings" and click "New". Enter the label (e.g., Event Name) and the Metadata Key (e.g., event). Select the source object, preferably a Blackthorn Payments object like Transaction. Choose the specific field from the Transaction object to map (e.g., a custom field named Event). Implementing the Mapping : After saving the mapping, add the metadata field to the relevant object?s page layout. If using a custom field, ensure it is populated either through a flow or other automation. Testing the Mapping : Conduct a test transaction to verify that the metadata appears correctly in Stripe. Check the metadata section in Stripe to ensure the custom field data is transferred.
Content Conclusion Text:
Mapping Salesforce metadata to Stripe enhances your transaction processing by ensuring that all relevant data is transferred seamlessly. This feature supports advanced reporting, better customer insights, and streamlined data management, providing a robust solution for integrating Salesforce with Stripe. 
 Pro Tips Review Field Relevance : Only map fields that provide value for your reporting and analytics to keep metadata concise. Regular Updates : Periodically review and update your mappings to ensure they align with your evolving business needs. Testing : Conduct thorough testing after setting up mappings to verify data accuracy. 
 Additional Resources Stripe Metadata Documentation

Content: Content Name: Guide to Configuring Stripe Webhooks for Blackthorn Payments
Content Introduction Text:
Introduction This guide will walk you through the comprehensive process of configuring Stripe webhooks for Blackthorn Payments. It includes creating a Force.com domain, setting up a site configuration, assigning site guest user permissions, and finally configuring the webhooks in Stripe. 
 What are Webhooks? Webhooks are automated messages sent from one app to another when a specific event occurs. They allow applications to communicate in real-time, instantly sending data to other systems without polling. 
 Benefits of Setting Up Webhooks Real-Time Updates: Automatically receive updates as soon as events happen, ensuring your system stays current. Efficient Communication: Reduce the need for frequent API calls, saving resources and improving performance. Enhanced Integration: Seamlessly connect different systems, allowing for better data flow and operational efficiency. Automation: Streamline processes by triggering automated workflows based on specific events. ? Steps to Setup Step 1: Create a Force.com Domain First, you need to create a Force.com domain to expose Salesforce data externally. Navigate to Salesforce Setup: In Salesforce, click on the gear icon and select "Setup." Search for Sites: Enter "Sites" in the Quick Find box and select "Sites." Register Your Domain: Click "New" to create a new site. Enter a Site Label, Site Name, and a Default Web Address. (We suggest using "webhook" or "stripe" for the Site Label and Site Name.) Set Active = "TRUE". For the Active Site Home Page field, click the Lookup icon and select "InMaintenance". (The page is not visible. It's just a placeholder because a value is required). Click Save. Step 2: Change the Default Record Owner for Webhook Events Go to Setup.  In the Quick Find box, enter and click ?Sites.?  Click Edit next to your webhook site. Change the Default Record Owner to a user of your choice. Click Save. Step 3: Assign Site Guest User Permission Set Assign the appropriate permission sets to the site guest user to ensure they have access to the necessary objects and fields. Navigate to Public Access Settings: From your site details page, click "Public Access Settings." Click the View Users or Assign Users button. Click the link for the site guest user. Assign Permission Sets: Under "Permission Set Assignments," click "Edit Assignments." Select "Blackthorn | Payments Site Guest User" then click "Save." Step 4: Configure Stripe Gateway for Webhooks Go to your payment gateway record Find the field 'Webhook Label' Place any value that you wish to set as your webhook label. You will use this in step 5. Step 5: Configure Stripe Webhooks Finally, set up Stripe webhooks to communicate with your Salesforce environment. Log into Stripe: Go to your Stripe dashboard and navigate to Developers > Webhooks. Add Endpoint: Click "Add endpoint" and enter the endpoint URL for your Salesforce site. This should be in the format https://[your-domain].force.com/[your-site-label]/services/apexrest/[your-webhook-label] . Select Events: Choose the events you want Stripe to notify your endpoint about, we recommend all events. ?
Content Conclusion Text:
By following these steps, you can ensure a seamless integration between Stripe and Salesforce, allowing real-time updates and efficient payment processing. For additional help, refer to the provided links or contact Blackthorn support. 
 Additional Resources Creating a Force.com Domain Site Configuration Assigning Site Guest User Permission Set Configuring Stripe Webhooks

 Set Up the Component Update the Page Layout The BT Events Attendee Registration component can be added to the Contact, Lead, Attendee, and Event lightning pages.  Blackthorn App Configuration

Content Introduction Text:
Tabs within the "Messaging Admin" Page When we talk about "Tabs" within the Messaging Admin app, we're talking about the bar on the far left side of the page. 
 
 
 We'll refer to these tabs as follows: Folder - Admin Tab SMS Bubble - Message Balance Phone - Phone Numbers Magnifying glass - Phone Number Lookups Cog/Gear - Settings Since we started in the Admin tab, we'll focus on the other four tabs for the most part.

 The Message Balance Tab 
 Here, we can see our Message balance. You will see a comment about " Your message balance will reset to XXX on XX/XX/XXXX " This shows you when your Month of messages rolls over, your balance will update to reflect the new month starting. " Monthly Messages " is actually the balance of your total messages between now and the next time you pay your invoice. So, for example, if your contract were for 1,000 messages per month over the course of a year, the "Monthly Messages" would show 12,000 your information will be updated based on your billing cycle. " Anytime Messages " is a buffer that we provide in case you go a little over your limit. You can purchase more of those using the "Add Messages" button For instance, if you're having a huge event this month and need more messages for this month, you can purchase additional anytime messages to cover this use when you need them The Phone Number Tab We already saw the ability to choose/add phone numbers from this tab, but there's more that we can do with each of our phone numbers! "Display Name" ?For any of your phone numbers, you can set the display name that will be used for that Phone Number. This will be seen when you interact with that Phone number within your Salesforce Org. Some examples of the way this is used are Jared Kirk's phone number Marketing Phone Number Campaign Phone Number "Call Forwarding" ? It's inevitable that some people try to call the number they've been texting. Rather than give those people an error, you can set up each texting number to have a number to forward any calls to. "After-Hour Response" ?If people text during your off-hours, you can set up an auto-reply to let them know you're out at the moment but will get back to them. You can also set up the Business Hours from within that setting. "Ownership Routing" ?This setting lets you decide who 'owns' the conversations that this phone number has. Related Record Owner is a great option if you have your phone number set up as a general number, and that way the conversation is 'owned' by whomever owns the account, contact, lead, etc. Last Sent Message Owner is great if you just want the conversation ownership to be based on who was active last. User/Queue is a great choice if you have a phone number set up for a specific person only. 
 The Phone Number Lookup Tab From this tab, we can learn about and interact with Phone Number lookups. The purpose of these is to make sure you're not using your purchased messages on phone numbers belonging to landlines and fax machines. 
 
 The Settings Tab This is where most of the magic happens! 
 In the Settings tab, we've got some 'tabs within tabs" 
 
 Under the " Configuration Settings>General " Tab, we have the option to Enable Campaigns (a Blackthorn Messaging feature we'll go over in the features content later) Turn on trackable links (shortens URLs and makes them trackable) Add messages to Contact records when a lead is converted. The " Configuration Settings>Message " tab gives you control over Inbound and Outbound message settings. Inbound Auto-Create Leads Post Incoming messages to Chatter Control over What Salesforce Object an incoming text can be related to if it's not a part of a conversation already. Conversation Timeframe Outbound Attach Outbound Images Consent Settings This is where you determine how often the Consent message goes out, and what yours looks like. The " Configuration Settings >TO Phone Number " tab is where you decide what objects and fields the Blackthorn Messaging App is looking at to find phone numbers. 
 The " Configuration Settings >Scheduled Jobs " tab is where you can enable the Schedule SMS feature to schedule text messages to go out at a specific time. IF you want to use this feature, make sure you click on the "START" button next to the "Blackthorn Messaging Messanger Scheduler" Job.

Content Introduction Text:
What is A2P Verification? A2P (Application to Person) Verification is a process that Mobile Phone Carriers require from Applications texting People to confirm that the number is not being used to spam or contact without consent. Blackthorn uses the carrier Twilio, and they have a page about A2P as well.  Feel free to check it out! 
 Why do I need A2P Verification? All carriers require A2P verification before they will let you register or use a phone number with them- so until you're verified, you won't be able to do any REAL messaging outside of some testing with our Demo mode test phone numbers. 
 
 How do we handle A2P Verification? We handle A2P verification in the Blackthorn Messaging app to keep things as simple as possible. If you're on the Blackthorn Admin tab, click on the "Account Activation" line in the "Account Setup Progress" box. 
 
 Once you've clicked into this box, you'll get a pop-up. This pop-up will have four pages of information that it will request: General Business Information This page just asks about addresses and basic company information. Business Entity Information This page is a bit more in-depth. To proceed, you will need your Business Registration Number (EIN, CBN, ACN, etc.). Usage & Consent This is by far the most important page in the A2P registration. Message Volume is your MONTHLY volume. Use Case will be how you plan to use your Messaging. Your Opt-In type needs some proof (except for Verbal). This is how you plan to get people to opt in to receive texts. Opt-in proof needs to have a URL that leads to something showing that you ask for consent to text someone. This can also include an explanation of how you obtain consent verbally or the process you use to obtain consent. Some of our Events customers have created an A2P content event and used a checkbox in a custom form that says something like, "By checking this box, you consent to receive text messages to the provided phone number from XXXX Co. for the purpose of XXXXXX and Event updates." It's always a good idea to link your privacy policy in your opt-in question too! Contact Information This needs to be two different people in the company who will just be verified as real people by Twilio. Review & Submit Just make sure everything looks good and submit! 
 As long as your Opt-in and information are good, the approval process usually takes 4-10 days from when you submit. 
 What can I do to make sure my A2P goes through without issue? 
 When Twilio is reviewing information to approve a messaging campaign (that's what they call your Messaging Account), they are also going to your website that you provide to make sure that you have a privacy policy that indicates what you plan to do with any information you have from customers (ie. text them with their phone number) 
 We often get errors or issues in the following areas when submitting A2P registration: 
 Compliant Privacy Policy "A compliant Privacy Policy must state that no mobile information will be shared with third parties/affiliates for marketing/promotional purposes. Information sharing to subcontractors in support services, such as customer service is permitted. All other use case categories exclude text messaging originator opt-in data and consent; this information will not be shared with any third parties." (You will be required to have an A2P-compliant Privacy Policy publically available on your website.  ( Check out Twilios documentation here   to see what is needed)  (Check out  Blackthorn's Privacy Policy  as an Example) 
 Sole Proprietor Companies We can still get these approved; we just need to know that's the circumstance 
 Legal Name & EIN Mismatch If the Legal name and EIN (Or other identification number) do not match federal (publically accessable) records, the approval will be rejected almost immediately. Please confirm before submitting: Legal Business Name: Legal name should be exactly as indicated in IRS CP-575 EIN/pre-Confirmation Letter Business Registration Number: Enter the EIN / Tax ID as it appears in the EIN listing You can also feel free to include a link to the reference documents if you would like. 
 Other General Registration Issues to be aware of The more you know, the better prepared you can be.
Content Conclusion Text: After you're A2P Verified We'll let you know once we've received word from Twilio that you're approved or if there was an issue that requires re-submission.

 You'll click the "Add Phone Numbers" button and select your Country and the Area code (or pattern) for which you want to find a number. As soon as you hit "Search," you'll see a list of available phone numbers for you to choose from.

 A Conversation in Blackthorn Messaging is a container for a group of text messages. They allow you to easily keep track of your inbound messages and manage which have been responded to and which are awaiting a reply. 
 Conversations are also great for collaborating teams with real-time updates, if one team member is replying to a conversation other team members will see this in real time.

Content Introduction Text:
What are Invoices for Event Checkout Invoices generated during event checkout are a way to keep track of money for paid events. All Event checkouts generate an invoice record to keep a complete and accurate record of the people who've gone through the checkout process. 
 Fortunately, you'll mostly not need to do much to interact with this object since it's generated by Blackthorn's automation at checkout.

What is Registration cancellation? Occasionally, our Attendees need to back out of an event they've signed up for. We hate to see it, but to make sure our records are accurate, it's best to give them the option to cancel their registration! 
 Blackthorn has a built-in solution for this. From the Event Settings, you can determine if any of your events should allow cancellation. If you choose to turn this feature on, your attendees will be able to cancel their registration from their AttendeeLink rather than needing to reach out to you. Content: Content Name: Learn how to Navigate the Mobile Payments App
Content Introduction Text:
How do I navigate the Mobile Payments App? 
 The Mobile Payments app includes a navigation menu to access different sections in the application. 
 
 
 
 Home This is the main screen of the application where users enter details about their Transactions and associate them with an Account and/or a Contact. 
 
 
 Tokenize Card This section of the application allows users to enter credit card details. The information is then tokenized and added to Salesforce as a Payment Method, which can be associated with an Account and/or a Contact. 
 
 
 The Payment Gateway selected on the Home screen will be the Payment Gateway you see populated on the Payment Method that is created through this Tokenize method. 
 Reader The Reader page allows users to connect the Mobile Payments app to a card reader. This is also where you can update the firmware of your card reader. When searching for a card reader, it may take up to two to three minutes for it to appear on the screen. Mobile Payments will search for firmware updates each time you connect a card reader. If your reader needs an update, an install link will be presented. Otherwise, a message stating that your reader has the latest update will be displayed. 
 
 
 Support The Support page allows users to contact our Customer Success team. This is where they can submit a case or access our documentation. 
 
 
 About The About page will display the app version. This can be helpful for troubleshooting, or if you want to check that you've installed the latest version. 
 
 
 Logout This is the basic option for logging out of the app.
Content Conclusion Text: You can visit our Documentation page for more information
