What Configuration Options do I have? 
 Lock an Amount On a Salesforce Transaction record, if you set the  Mobile Lock Amount  = "Yes", the Mobile Payments app will not allow the  Amount  value to be changed for that Transaction. 
 Skip the Intro Screen On a Salesforce Transaction record, if you set the  Mobile Skip Intro Screen  = "Yes", the Mobile Payments app will not show the Intro screen (Description, Amount, Currency, etc) for that Transaction. 
 Set Payment Methods If values are set on the Transaction record  Accepted Payment Methods  field or the Payment Gateway record  Accepted Payment Methods  field, only the set Payment Methods will be available for the selected Payment Gateway or Transaction. 
 The Accepted Payment Methods fields are evaluated in the following order: If the Transaction  Accepted Payment Methods  field is set, use those values for the Transaction. Otherwise, if the Payment Gateway  Accepted Payment Methods  field is set, use those values for the Transaction. If neither of those fields are set, all Payment Methods are available for use. Require an Existing Transaction for Mobile The ?Require Existing Transaction for Mobile? feature is supported in the Mobile Payments app for Android devices. This setting blocks users from processing a payment in the Mobile Payments app if there isn?t an existing Transaction in Salesforce before the app is launched.

Content Introduction Text:
Ensuring compliance with SMS regulations is essential for maintaining trust and avoiding legal issues. Blackthorn Messaging makes it easy to set up automated responses for help and stop messages. This guide will walk you through the configuration process to ensure your messaging adheres to best practices. 
 Steps to Configure Help and Stop Messages Access Phone Number Record: Navigate to the Blackthorn Messaging admin tab. Click "Manage Phone Numbers" and select the phone number you want to configure. Set Up Help and Stop Messages: In the phone number record, locate the "Compliance Messages" section. Enter your customized response in the "Help Message" field. This will be sent when a recipient texts ?HELP? or ?INFO? to your number. Enter your customized response in the "Stop Message" field. This will be sent when a recipient texts ?STOP,? ?END,? ?QUIT,? ?CANCEL,? or ?UNSUBSCRIBE.? Save the Configuration: Once your messages are set, click "Save." The configured messages are now tied to the specific phone number. Automated Compliance Handling: When a recipient texts ?STOP,? Blackthorn Messaging will automatically update the ?Do Not SMS? field on the related contact, account, or lead, ensuring they are excluded from future bulk messaging.
Content Conclusion Text:
Configuring help and stop messages in Blackthorn Messaging is crucial for staying compliant with SMS regulations. Following these steps will ensure your recipients can easily manage their communication preferences. 
 Pro Tips Customization: Update placeholders in the default messages to match your company?s details. Multiple Numbers: Each phone number can have unique help and stop messages. 
 FAQs Q: What happens when someone sends STOP? A: The contact is automatically marked as ?Do Not SMS,? preventing future messages. 
 Q: Can I use different messages for different numbers? A: Yes, each phone number can have its own help and stop messages. 
 Additional Resources Blackthorn Help and Stop Message Compliance Documentation

Content Introduction Text:
Campaign response rules in Blackthorn Messaging allow you to automate conversations within your campaigns, capture lead information, and manage interactions efficiently. This guide will walk you through the steps to set up and configure these rules. 
 Steps to Configure Campaign Response Rules Adjust Campaign Page Layout: Navigate to the Campaign object in Salesforce. Edit the page layout by adding the ?Send SMS Response Rules? button. Add fields like Phone Number, Phone Number Display, SMS Keyword, and Enforce Single Conversation to the layout. Create SMS Templates: Go to the SMS Templates section and create templates for the leads or contacts you?ll be working with. For each template, specify the text message content and use merge fields to personalize the messages. Set Up SMS Response Rules: Go to your campaign and click on ?SMS Response Rules.? Create rules that determine the sequence of messages sent based on user responses. Specify what information to capture (e.g., name, email) from each response. Save the rules to finalize the setup. Configure Additional Settings: Assign a phone number for the campaign and set the SMS Keyword. Decide whether to enforce single conversations, which limits recipients to receiving automated responses only once. Enable Auto-Create Leads: In the Admin tab, enable the ?Auto Create Leads? checkbox to automatically create a lead if a new phone number interacts with your campaign.
Content Conclusion Text:
Campaign response rules in Blackthorn Messaging are a powerful tool for automating interactions and capturing lead data. By following these steps, you can streamline your campaigns and enhance your CRM processes. 
 Pro Tips Customization: Tailor SMS templates and response rules to fit your specific campaign needs. Automation: Use automation rules to route captured information into your CRM effectively.

What Is Authenticated iframe? The Authenticated iframe feature allows you to securely embed content within an iframe on your website or application. This feature ensures that users are authenticated before accessing specific data by linking them to their Salesforce Contact ID. This setup controls visibility and pre-populates information, streamlining user interactions while maintaining security.

 Why on earth would I want to use this feature instead of a normal iframe? 
 Setting up an Authenticated iframe, rather than a standard one, provides enhanced security and personalized user experiences. By ensuring that only authenticated users can access specific content, you protect sensitive data and ensure that users see only the information relevant to them. Additionally, it allows for seamless integration with Salesforce, auto-filling forms and streamlining user interactions, ultimately improving the overall user experience and reducing the potential for errors. Use Cases I have a customer portal and want to offer my logged-in users the ability to register for events with their information automatically pre-filled based on their Salesforce Contact ID. I manage a secure membership site and need to display specific content or event registrations that only authenticated users can access, ensuring that sensitive information is protected. How Do I Get Started setting up an Authenticated iframe? The specific steps are found in our documentation, but generally, these are the steps you'll take to set up your Authenticated iframe. 
 Host Authentication Protocol: Set up your authentication on your website. Generate Context Key: Create and encode a secure Context Key. Send Context Key to Blackthorn: Email the Context Key to admin@blackthorn.io for setup. Embed the iframe: Embed the Blackthorn Events app using an iframe. Integrate SSO Code: Encrypt the Contact ID with the Context Key. Configure Visibility: Control content visibility using Contact IDs. For detailed instructions, refer to the Authentication via iframe Documentation . Sub-Features Visibility Control Control which contacts can see specific event details based on their Salesforce Contact ID. Seamless Integration Integrate with existing authentication systems to provide a smooth and secure user experience. Information Pre-Population Using the Authenticated iframe will allow you to pass the contact information of the user to Salesforce/Blackthorn and allow for some of the basic information to pre-fill based on the user's Contact record. FAQ?s Question: Do I need to generate an SSO code for each contact? Answer: Yes, a unique SSO code must be generated for each contact to ensure they are properly authenticated before accessing the iframe content. 
 Question: Can I use third-party authentication protocols with the Authenticated iframe? Answer: Yes, you can integrate the iframe with third-party authentication protocols like OpenID or Okta, though you will need to manage the custom coding for this integration. Content: Content Name: Payment Processing and Tax in Blackthorn Events
Content Introduction Text:
Introduction Fees, such as payment processing and tax, are useful for event organizers to cover extra costs when participants register for events. Blackthorn Events makes it easy to apply these fees automatically at checkout, either as additional charges or through tax-inclusive pricing. This guide will show you how to set up both types of fees efficiently. 
 Steps to Set Up Fees Configure a Payment Processing Fee: Navigate to Blackthorn Events in Salesforce and open the event. In the event setup, locate the Fees section. To create a payment processing fee, click "New Fee," assign a name (e.g., "Card Fee"), and set the percentage. Mark it as a default fee if you want this fee applied automatically. Set Up a Tax Fee: Similarly, create a tax fee by selecting "Tax" as the fee type. You can configure this to be calculated at checkout or as tax-inclusive pricing. If you choose tax-inclusive pricing, the total price will include tax from the start. Otherwise, the tax will be calculated and added during checkout. Test the Setup: Create a test registration to ensure the correct fees are applied. If using card payments, the payment processing fee will show, and if a tax fee is applied, it will be visible at checkout. Exclude Tax for Specific Tickets: Some tickets can be excluded from tax fees. Select the ticket and mark it as tax-exempt in the event item settings.
Content Conclusion Text:
Setting up payment processing and tax fees in Blackthorn Events ensures that your event covers all costs associated with payment processing and tax compliance. By following these steps, you can automate fee application for smooth and transparent pricing at checkout. 
 FAQs Question: Can I apply both a processing fee and tax? Answer: Yes, you can apply both. The processing fee covers payment gateway charges, and the tax fee applies the relevant tax at checkout. 
 Question: How do I exclude a specific ticket from tax fees? Answer: Mark the ticket as ?Tax Exempt? under the event item settings. 
 Additional Resources Blackthorn Events Fee Setup Documentation

Content: Content Name: Managing Event Seating with Blackthorn's Table Manager
Content Introduction Text:
Introduction Blackthorn?s Table Manager simplifies organizing and assigning seating for events. This feature enables event organizers to easily manage attendee assignments to tables, improving event coordination. It allows you to create tables, assign seats, and adjust seating arrangements efficiently within Salesforce. 
 Steps to Set Up Table Manager Add Table Manager to Event Page: Go to the event?s page and click the gear icon to edit the page. In the Lightning builder, add a new tab labeled "Table Manager."  Pro Tips Event Size: If your event exceeds 100 tables or 10 seats per table, you?ll need to manage seating manually. Internal Use: Table Manager is for internal event organization only and has no front-facing functionality.

Blackthorn?s Table Manager simplifies seating management for events, streamlining the assignment process and ensuring all records are updated in Salesforce for better tracking and reporting. Organizers can focus on creating memorable experiences without getting bogged down by logistical challenges.

🧭 COM Navigation 
 Our COM (Customer Onboarding Management) record contains a lot of data and was born out of a desire to see everything (or at least almost everything) related to a new customer's onboarding project in one central place. 
 Here's an image of a typical COM record with several areas highlighted that will be explaind below. Worth noting is that the layout shown here has the most information on it. Some record types will remove some of these fields that are not helpful for that specific record type. 
 🖼? COM Record Overview 
 
 🔑 Key Sections in the COM Record 1?? Project Information Section This area contains key details from the Account and Closed/Won Opportunity , such as: Customer Name Yearly Contract Value Timeline , Business Impact , and Requirements passed on by the AE who made the sale. The Onboarding Status field is partially automated based on the Project Start Date and Go-Live Dates . Note : This should only be updated manually if the project is Cancelled . 2?? Project Overview Panel Provides a day-by-day view of what's happening in the Onboarding Project . During the Pre-Onboarding Stage (for customers who purchased the Events App), you?ll see the customer's Pre-Onboarding Survey results. This section includes: Basic info about the last interaction with the customer Next steps in the onboarding process Any concerns or "bad feelings" based on customer interaction. Assignment Completion % : Shows the average percentage of assignments completed by anyone linked to this COM record. Also includes a direct link to the Community COM Record page (requires the customer to be logged in). 3?? Update Support Notes Flow This ScreenFlow helps update Support Notes for the customer?s account. The Support Notes field ensures the support team is aware of any relevant info when working on a case. If notes already exist on the account, they will show up in this ScreenFlow, and you can update them by clicking the Update button. 4?? Contacts Tab Displays helpful info from the Closed/Won Opportunity about the customer?s team, including: Technical Contact Project Sponsor (referred to as the Stakeholder on the Opportunity) Partner and Partner Contact As the Onboarding Manager identifies the Project Manager and Executive Sponsor , these fields are updated. Tip : Help text is available for each role to clarify their definitions. 5?? EduGuide Assignment Tool This is a ScreenFlow used to create EduGuide assignments related to this COM for anyone linked to either the Account or Partner Account . More details about this flow are available in the COM Flows lesson. 6?? System Information This section includes basic info with a few important fields: Production Org ID and Sandbox Org ID : Entering values here will search for any licenses related to the Org IDs, updating them on the account or creating a new Sandbox Account , and linking them to the COM. Pro Tip : If the customer has more than one Sandbox or Dev account, update and save the Org IDs one at a time. Apps Purchased : Shows the apps purchased within the related Closed/Won Opportunity. Payment Gateway : If filled in on the Opportunity, it maps to this field. Otherwise, use this field to indicate the customer's payment gateway. Stripe Gateway Customer : If the Apps Purchased includes Messaging , this field shows the Stripe Customer ID , which is used to activate the messaging account. 7?? COM Stage The COM Stage is defaulted to "Pre-Onboarding" when the COM is created. This field tracks the customer's progress through the onboarding process, with different values based on the Record Type . Note : Stages are not automated and should be manually updated by the Onboarding Manager. 📌 Related List Quick Links 8?? Quick Access to Related Objects Learning Paths : (DEPRECATED) Onboarding Events : Meetings with the customer that should be visible in the Community. Some meetings are auto-created based on the COM Record Type , but additional meetings can be added manually. Notes & Attachments : Files attached to Chatter posts land here. Licenses : All licenses related to the Org IDs in the System Information fields are displayed here. Assignments : Shows all EduGuide assignments linked to the COM record. Cases : Only cases created during the onboarding project are shown. Engagements : Lists customer engagements with EduGuide content. CX Time Tracking : Stores final meeting info (not visible to the customer). Typeform Responses : Usually contains the Pre-Onboarding Survey. Customer Onboarding Management History : Tracks updates to key fields, such as project dates. Technical Audits : Shows any technical audits performed during onboarding or re-enablement (typically only applicable to Re-Enablement Record Types ). 
 
 In some of these areas, we have additional tabs that will show more information 
 
 📅 Project Dates Tab (Item 1) The Second tab is "Project Dates". On this tab, you will find the "Onboarding Events," which has the meeting dates (which need to be manually added when you schedule the meetings) and recording links for the meetings (Again, Manually added after the meeting) Also visible on this tab are the "Base Project Start Dates on" field. The field is set to "Planned Go-Live Date": the planned go-live date is used for the source of truth (Days Remaining, and a few other fields) The field is set to "Project Start Date": This is typically used with a Deferred Start onboarding (Meaning they do not want to start the Blackthorn Onboarding right away- maybe we're a smaller part of a larger project). In this case, we get a few additional fields to interact with. "Project Start Date" can be set to the date they want to start the project or is automatically set based on the Pre-Onboarding Survey. "Ideal Go-Live" is an estimate of when they will go live based on the start date. This field equals the Project Start Date + Ideal Onboarding Weeks. "Ideal Onboarding Weeks" is defaulted to (7), and reflects a rough average of what we would call "Normal" onboardings. ? The last tab here is "Chatter," which should be self-evident. 
 
 👤 Contacts Tab (Blackthorn Team) (Item 4) Found alongside the Customer Team information, you will also find information about the Blackthorn team. 
 Blackthorn Team The Account Executive is the AE who owned the Opportunity The Onboarding Manager is the OBM who is responsible for this COM (Selected by Round Robin flow) The Customer Success Manager is the Owner of the Account (Updates when the owner is moved from the AE to the CSM) Support Primary and Support Secondary are the Support Reps assigned to this Account (Not all accounts have this) The project Sponsor is always Ashley, as she is the head of the CSX Department. 
 
 📊 Fields for CSM Tab (Item 2) ? This tab is found in the "Project Overview" section. 
 These fields are available here at any time but also appear in the "Project Information" section as the onboarding approaches Completion. Onboarding Pain Points : This should represent the issues that the customer experienced and may reference as difficulties in the Onboarding process. i.e. lots of cases, support deemed insufficient, product gaps, etc. Personality Profiles : This would be a summary of the people that the OBM worked with- especially those who were either great to work with, or.... more difficult.

Content: Content Name: 'So you were assigned a COM Record...'
Content Introduction Text: ? Checklist for COM Record Creation When a COM (Customer Onboarding Management) record is created via a Closed/Won opportunity, there are a few important items to complete. Here's a brief overview: 📧 Email Notification Action : Watch for an automatic email that?s generated when the opportunity is marked as 'Closed Won' and the COM record is created. 💬 Chatter Post Wait for it! : Keep an eye on the automatically generated Chatter posts, which prompt you to take necessary next steps. 📞 Sales Handoff Call Action : Schedule a call with the Customer Success Manager (CSM) and Account Executive (AE) to discuss onboarding requirements and project details. 📝 Update "What Did You Purchase?" Action : Retrieve contract details and update this field with specific information about the licenses or features purchased (e.g., users, events, registrations, support plan). 📝 Survey Responses Wait for it! : Monitor responses to the Pre-Onboarding Survey . Pay attention to updates in the project start date, production org ID, and sandbox org ID. 👥 Team Assignments Action : Confirm that both the Blackthorn and customer teams are accurately listed and assigned. 🔧 Installation/Configuration Tasks Action : Verify that assignments for installation and configuration are properly assigned. Also, confirm whether community users were created for the technical and partner contacts. 📋 Customer Familiarization Action : Review the AE notes to gain insight into the customer's goals and needs to better tailor the onboarding process.

As of late 2024, we have six Record Types for the COM object. All of these records use the sale "Page Layout" but have unique Lightning Page Layouts. 
 Dedicated Onboarding This record type is created when an Opportunity marked as Closed/Won has a 100k+ renewal ARR (or is a strategic Opportunity) and the customer has purchased the Events App. 
 Premier Onboarding This record type is created when an Opportunity that is marked as Closed/Won has between 13k - 100k Renewal ARR and they have purchased the Events App. 
 Standard Onboarding This record type is created when an Opportunity that is marked as Closed/Won has under 13k Renewal ARR and the customer has purchased the Events App. 
 Self Onboarding This record type is created when an Opportunity marked as Closed/Won has not purchased the Events App. This is because our Payments, Messaging, and Compliance apps are currently laid out as self-service, self-education onboarding. We still support these customers and offer help where it is needed, but they tend to be more hands-off. 
 Re-Enablement Sometimes referred to as "Re-Onboarding," this is typically the result of a customer who has had poor adoption or full staff turnover (which happens more often than we wish it did). 
 Customer Success As of October 2024, this is something that we are still ironing out. When an onboarding record is marked as "Completed", meaning the onboarding process Is complete and they are live- we have a flow in place that will update the Record type to "Customer Success" and update the owner of the record to the Customer Success Manager. 
 
 What's the difference? 
 Great question! The main onboarding record types ( Dedicated, Premier, Standard, and Self-Onboarding ) have very few differences; we mainly use the record types for record keeping. 
 If you set the Record type to " Re-Enablement, " it will remove several fields needed for typical onboarding. This record type is focused on re-education and will likely center around a Tech-Audit, "Assignments," and customer meetings in an "Events Sprint" to help get them up to speed and answer all their questions. 
 A note on the Re-Enablement Record type and setting them up is that if you go to the Account, go to the COM-related list, create a new one, and just save it without updating any fields; we have a flow in place that will fill in much of the useful information so you don't have to go through and fill it all in yourself! 
 The Customer Success Record type is the most unique, as the CSM does not need many of the fields that are used during Onboarding. This Record type Shows mostly the Customer Information and the Use and Use Case information gathered in Onboarding in the main area and removes some of the unneeded components. The second tab in the Customer Success main section has also been updated to show the CX time Tracking flow, which is similar to what they would find on the Account page.
Content Conclusion Text: 🗂 Record Types for the COM Object (As of Late 2024) All of the following record types share the same Page Layout but have unique Lightning Page Layouts : 🔹 Dedicated Onboarding Created when an Opportunity marked as Closed/Won has a 100k+ renewal ARR (or is a strategic Opportunity), and the customer has purchased the Events App . 🔸 Premier Onboarding Created when an Opportunity marked as Closed/Won has a 13k - 100k Renewal ARR , and the customer has purchased the Events App . 🔹 Standard Onboarding Created when an Opportunity marked as Closed/Won has an ARR under 13k , and the customer has purchased the Events App . 🔸 Self Onboarding Created when an Opportunity marked as Closed/Won and the customer has not purchased the Events App . Note : Payments, Messaging, and Compliance apps are generally laid out as self-service, self-education onboarding . We still support these customers but with a more hands-off approach. 🔹 Re-Enablement (Re-Onboarding) Used for customers with poor adoption or full staff turnover . Focuses on: Tech-Audit Assignments Customer meetings in an "Events Sprint" to help them catch up. Setup Tip : If you create a new Re-Enablement record and save it without updating any fields, a flow will automatically fill in most of the useful information. 🔸 Customer Success Created when an onboarding record is marked as "Completed" (i.e., the customer is live). A flow updates the Record Type to "Customer Success" and assigns the record to the Customer Success Manager (CSM) . 🔍 What?s the Difference? The main onboarding record types ( Dedicated , Premier , Standard , and Self-Onboarding ) differ only slightly. They are primarily used for record keeping. 🛠 Re-Enablement Record Type Removes several fields typically needed for onboarding and centers around re-education . Focuses on Tech-Audit , Assignments , and Events Sprint meetings to answer customer questions and get them back on track. 🔑 Customer Success Record Type The CSM doesn't need many of the fields used during onboarding, so this record type primarily shows: Customer Information Use and Use Case Information gathered during onboarding. The second tab has been updated to display the CX Time Tracking flow , similar to the layout on the Account page .

Flows for COM Records We use several Flows to automate and simplify interactions with COM records. For more details, check out the 'COM Flows' lesson, but here?s a high-level overview of the key processes. 📝 COM Creation A COM is automatically created when an Opportunity is marked as Closed/Won under one of two conditions: The Opportunity Type is listed as "Initial ." The Opportunity has the checkbox "Onboarding Needed?" checked (only available for AE on Expansion deals). ?? Troubleshooting : If a COM is created or not created in error, it?s usually because one of these conditions was applied incorrectly. ?? What Happens When a COM is Created Once a COM is created, several automations kick in to set up key details: Apps Purchased Flow : Automatically evaluates the "Apps Purchased" field and creates assignments for the Technical or Partner Contact to install/configure those apps. Onboarding Payment Gateway : If the Onboarding Payment Gateway field is filled out on the Opportunity, it will be added to the System Information section in the COM. Onboarding Type : If populated on the Opportunity (usually for strategic deals), this field overrides the default Record Type. Project Information : Fields in this section are populated from the Opportunity that generated the COM. CSM Assignment : The CSM field in the Blackthorn Team section is initially empty. Once the Account Owner is updated to a CSM, this field will be filled. Messaging App Activation : If the customer purchased the Messaging App , the Stripe CustomerID (from the Account) will populate in the System Information section, which we use to activate the messaging account. 📅 Project Dates Setup When a COM is created, the Project Dates tab will include default information: "Base Project Start Dates on" : Set to "Planned Go Live Date" . Planned GO Live Date : Automatically set to COM Creation Date + 49 days (7 weeks). 🚦 Pre-Onboarding Stage & Survey For customers who purchased Events and are in the Pre-Onboarding stage: You will see the Pre-Onboarding Survey Results . After the customer completes the survey, the results fields will be populated, and a Chatter post will summarize their answers. Org IDs will be updated in the System Information Section based on the survey response. This will also relate the licenses to the Account, and COM project. if the Sandbox OrgID is provided, it will create a "Sandbox" account as a child account of the main account. PRO TIP : If the customer is using more than one Sandbox/Dev environment, you can add them one at a time, and the Licenses will be related and the Sandbox accounts will be created for each. 
 Deferred Onboarding : If the customer defers their onboarding start date in the survey, we update: "Base Project Start Dates On" = Project Start Date (the date they provided). The Planned Go-Live Date automatically updates only if it is set before the Project Start Date. (Start Date + 49) 🔄 Onboarding Events & Schedule Templates The Onboarding Events related list automatically creates template Onboarding Events based on the Onboarding Schedule Templates record. Onboarding Schedule Templates : This record is where we add, update, or remove typical Onboarding Events for new onboardings. 🚥 Onboarding Status Updates The Onboarding Status in the Project Information section updates automatically based on the Planned Go-Live Date and Project Start Dates . 🕒 Onboarding Status Daily Automation at 11:45 PM EST Every day at around 11:45 PM EST , a Flow evaluates COM records: Late : If the Planned Go-Live Date is in the past, the status is updated to "Late" . On Hold : If the Project Start Date is in the future, the status is set to "On Hold" . On Time : If the Project Start Date is today, the status is set to "On Time." Important : If the status is set to "On Hold" , no other automation will update the status unless the Project Start Date changes. 🔔 Chatter Notifications Chatter notifications are triggered based on Project Dates and sent to the Onboarding Manager. These can be seen in the COM Chatter Notifications object and are triggered based on combinations of: App Purchased Project Dates Project Start Date Onboarding Start Date (COM creation date) Planned Go-Live Date

What is Advanced Visibility? Advanced Visibility is a powerful feature allowing your team to precisely control visibility and access to your Events, Event Items and Sessions. You can now setup custom criteria using any field on the Contact or Person Account object to gate access to any part of your event. 
 Already utilize Visibility Control today? No problem, just use the Visibility Control field in your BT Rule and it will work seamlessly with any other criteria you define! 
 Examples: We're hosting a class of 2005 Reunion, I can setup a BT Rule so that only Contacts or Person Accounts with a Class Year of 2005 can see this event. 
 For a Homecoming event, you can use a BT Rule to ensure that your Board of Advisors can register for a private session.
Content Conclusion Text:
Notes: Using the Refresh Rule Button will push updates to your Rules and changes will reflect on your event pages in 1-2 minutes. Otherwise we have a scheduled job that runs 60 minutes after a rule is created or updated. 
 FAQs Question: What if I can't create BT rules in my org? Answer: Before using Advanced Visibility you will need to have Caching 2.0 enabled in your org and reach out to Blackthorn Support as we will need to activate this feature for your org. 
 Question: Can I use Advanced Visibility for Public facing (non-authenticated) events? Answer: You can setup a BT Rule on an Event item or Session for a public event. However the item with the BT Rule set would be hidden on the public page and only be visible to authenticated users the rule applies to. 
 
 Question: Does Advanced Visibility work with Express Registration ? Answer: Yes! You can also use the "Extend Visibility to Account" and "Extend Eligibility to Account" fields to allow users to quickly register other related contacts to a restricted event. 
 Question: Do I need an Experience Cloud site to use Advanced Visibility? Answer: While Advanced Visibility does require users to be authenticated you aren't required to use an Experience Cloud site. You can also use an Authenticated Iframe . 
 Question: I already use Visibility Controls, can I still use Advanced Visibility? Answer: Yes! Visibility Controls on the Attendee object will still function and are able to be used with AttendeeLink invites. For use with Advanced Visibility you would need to set your BT Rule to reference the Visibility Control Field on the Contact/Person Account along with any other criteria you need.

What is a Salesforce Object? 📂 In Salesforce, an Object is like a storage container that holds information about a specific type of data, similar to a table in a database. It organizes data to support your business processes. You can think of Objects as folders that hold all the related records for a particular type of information. 
 For example: The Event Object in Blackthorn stores all the key details about an event, such as its name, date, location, and capacity. The Attendee Object holds data for each person registered to attend the event. 
 Objects can be Standard (like Accounts, Contacts, and Leads, which Salesforce provides by default) or Custom (like Event or Attendee, created specifically for Blackthorn?s needs). Custom Objects allow us to capture details unique to our app, helping you manage events and registrations more effectively. 
 
 
 
 Why Objects Matter: Objects help you organize and access information efficiently. In Blackthorn, they enable you to track event details, manage attendees, and maintain organized records, simplifying event planning and reporting. Think of each Object as a tool that gathers all relevant data in one place, so you can focus on what matters without hunting through scattered information. 
 
 
 Key Features of Objects 💡 Data Organization: Objects group related data together, making it easy to access and manage. For example, all your event data lives in the Event Object. Customizability: With Custom Objects, Blackthorn tailors Salesforce to meet your specific needs, allowing you to store exactly the information your business requires. Data Relationships: Objects can be linked to each other, helping you track relationships across your records. For instance, each Attendee Record is connected to an Event Record, giving you a complete view of who is attending each event. 
 How to View Objects in Salesforce 🔍 App Launcher: To access different Objects, use the App Launcher in the upper left corner of Salesforce. Just type the Object name (like "Events") in the search bar. Navigation Bar: Once in the Blackthorn app, you'll see tabs for different Objects in the navigation bar, such as Events, Attendees, or Payments. Each tab takes you to the records stored in that Object. Note for Admins: If you need custom Objects to meet unique business needs, you can create them through Setup > Object Manager. Just ensure you have the necessary permissions to customize data structures in Salesforce. 
 Pro Tips 💼 Customization: Tailor Objects by adding relevant Fields, adjusting Page Layouts, or creating Related Lists to suit your workflow. Easy Access: Use List Views within an Object to filter and display only the data you need, such as a list of upcoming events or registered attendees.
Content Conclusion Text:
FAQs ? Q: Can I add my own fields to an Object? A: Yes, admins can customize Objects by adding new fields to capture specific information. For example, you might add a 'Preferred Contact Method' field to the Attendee Object. Q: How do I find specific records within an Object? A: Use List Views and Filters within each Object to narrow down records based on criteria, such as event date or attendee registration status. 
 
 
 Conclusion 🎉 Understanding Objects is fundamental to using Salesforce effectively. In Blackthorn, Objects like Events and Attendees gather all relevant data into organized structures, making it easy to manage and retrieve information. Whether you're planning events or tracking attendance, Objects keep everything connected and accessible.

Content Introduction Text:
What is a Salesforce Field? 🔍 In Salesforce, a Field is like a column in a spreadsheet. Each field holds one type of information that is used across all entries (called ?records?) within a list, which Salesforce calls an ?Object.? 
 For example: The Event Date field in Blackthorn?s Event Object shows the date of an event. The Contact Email field in the Attendee Object holds each attendee?s email address. 
 Fields help organize the important details for each entry, making it easier to search for, sort, and report on specific information. 
 
 
 Key Things to Know About Fields 📝 Consistency: Fields make sure information is collected in the same way across entries, so it?s easier to understand and use later. Custom Fields: Your organization can add its own fields to track specific information. For example, a ?Preferred Session? field could help keep track of which event session an attendee wants to join. Field Types: Each field is designed to hold a certain kind of information, like text, dates, numbers, or dropdown choices. 
 
 
 How to See and Work with Fields in Salesforce 🛠? Viewing Fields: Open a record in an Object, like an Event or Attendee, to see the fields and details for that entry. Changing Fields: If a field needs to be changed or added, an admin can help make those updates. Fields are managed under Setup > Object Manager, where fields can be added, edited, or removed. 
 Note for Admins: Fields can be customized to fit what your organization needs to track. Make sure to pick the best field type (e.g., text or date) for the information. 
 
 
 Pro Tips 💡 Required Fields: Important fields, like ?Contact Phone? for attendees, can be set as required, meaning they must be filled out. Field Access: Not everyone can see or edit all fields. Your organization can choose who has access based on their role.
Content Conclusion Text:
FAQ?s Question: I can't edit a field; why? Answer: There are a few reasons you might not be able to edit a field: Permissions : You may not have permission to edit that field. Check with your admin to see if you have the right access. Read-Only Field : Some fields are set as read-only, meaning no one can edit them, or they can only be changed under certain conditions. Ask your admin to help check your permissions or field settings. 
 Question: I can't see a field that someone else can; why? Answer: You might not see a field for a few reasons: Permissions : You may not have permission to view the field. Your admin can check and update your access if needed. Page Layout : You might be using a different page layout where the field isn?t visible. Record Type : The field might only show on certain types of records, and yours might be different. Reach out to your admin to review your permissions or page layout. 
 
 Conclusion 🎉 Fields in Salesforce organize the important details that help you track the right information. By setting up custom fields and deciding who can view or edit them, you can make sure everyone has the information they need while keeping sensitive data protected.

Content Introduction Text:
What is a Salesforce Record? 📋 A Record in Salesforce is like a row in a spreadsheet. It holds all the details for a single entry in an Object, similar to a profile for one event, attendee, or other item in the system. 
 For example: Each Event record in Blackthorn?s Event Object might include information like the event?s name, date, and location. Each Attendee record in the Attendee Object holds information about one attendee, such as their name and contact information. 
 Each record brings together all the relevant details in one place, making it easier to track and manage information. 
 
 
 Key Things to Know About Records 📝 Uniqueness: Every record is unique and represents one specific entry in the system. Relationships: Records can connect to other records. For instance, an Attendee record might link to an Event record, helping you see which attendees registered for an event. Editing: You can view or update details in a record to keep information current, like updating an attendee?s contact info. 
 
 
 How to View and Edit Records in Salesforce 🛠? Viewing Records: Open an Object (like Events or Attendees) and click on a specific entry to see all its details. Editing Records: Within a record, you can update fields to keep the information accurate. Just click into the fields you want to change, make updates, and save. Note for Admins: Record details can be customized to include only the most relevant fields, ensuring a streamlined view for users. 
 
 
 Pro Tips 💡 Track History: You can set up certain fields to track history, so changes are logged over time. Record Security: Your organization can control who can view or edit specific records, keeping sensitive information secure.
Content Conclusion Text:
FAQs ? Q: Can I restore a deleted record? A: Yes, recently deleted records are stored in the Recycle Bin (like a trash folder) and can be restored if needed. Q: How can I see all related records? A: Use related lists within a record to see connected records, like seeing all attendees linked to an event. 
 
 ?Conclusion 🎉 Records in Salesforce bring together essential details for each item or person, helping you stay organized. With custom fields and security settings, you can tailor records to meet your organization?s needs while ensuring data stays protected.

Content Introduction Text:
What is a Salesforce List View? 📑 A List View in Salesforce is like a saved search or filtered list that displays only the records you need based on specific criteria. It?s a quick way to pull up data relevant to your task without sorting through all records. 
 For example: You might create a List View to show upcoming events so you can see only those scheduled soon. Or, a List View for attendees who?ve registered for an event, helping you quickly see who?s confirmed. 
 List Views streamline your work by letting you focus on the most relevant records. Key Things to Know About List Views 📝 Filters: Set filters to show only certain records, like active events or attendees registered for today?s session. Saving Views: Save your List Views for repeated use, so you can easily access them without reapplying filters. Sharing: You can set List Views as private, public, or shared with specific groups, controlling who can access them. How to Create and Use List Views in Salesforce 🛠? Creating a New List View: Open an Object (like Events or Attendees) and select ?Create New View.? Define the filters to display just the records you want. Using a Saved List View: Select any saved List View to instantly see its filtered results, like a list of ?All Upcoming Events.? Note for Admins: Use List View permissions to control access, helping team members focus on their most important records. Pro Tips 💡 Default Views: Set a default List View for each Object so users see their preferred view first. Pinned Views: Pin commonly used List Views to make them easy to find at the top of the page.
Content Conclusion Text: FAQs ? Q: Can I make my List View visible only to me? A: Yes, select ?Only I can see this view? when creating or editing your List View to keep it private. Q: How can I share my List View with my team? A: If allowed, set the List View?s visibility to public or restricted groups to ensure only the right people have access. Conclusion 🎉 List Views help you organize and display just the records you need, keeping your workflow efficient. By saving, customizing, and sharing views, you can quickly access important data and stay focused on what matters most.

Content Introduction Text: 🌟 What a Blackthorn Onboarding Journey Looks Like 🌟 An overview for internal teams and new employees 1. 🔔 Welcome & First Touchpoint Welcome Email : Once a new customer signs up, we send a welcome email with key resources, including an introductory video and access to the Blackthorn Customer Community . This is where they?ll find detailed onboarding instructions, assignments, and resources. Once the CSM is assigned to the Account, the Onboarding Manager will reach out Pre-Onboarding Survey : Customers are prompted to complete this survey to help us gather necessary details like project start dates, production org info, and sandbox org details. 2. 🛠 Internal Coordination: Sales Handoff Customer Onboarding Management (COM) Record : Once a Closed/Won opportunity is secured, a COM record is created. This triggers internal tasks for the onboarding team, including verifying contract details (e.g., "What Did You Purchase?" field) and confirming team assignments. Sales Handoff : The OBM will schedule an internal handoff call between the sales team and the CSM (Customer Success Manager) to align everyone on the customer?s specific goals and project details. (No technical teams involved here.) The expectation is to get this scheduled ASAP?try to schedule the Sales handoff the same day the deal closes. Once the Kickoff is completed, the OBM will need to reach out to the customer with a link to schedule a Kick-off call. You can use this template if you'd like- just make sure you replace the placeholder text. https://docs.google.com/document/d/18nsFXTX9ZkkOYAbRTZI4x0x8grpHKtEvGjkvX1ddPW4/edit?usp=sharing 3. 📞 Kick-off Call The Kick-off Call is scheduled with the customer?s team, CSM , and OBM . Sometimes the customer?s Salesforce implementation partner also joins. This call sets expectations, discusses timelines, and introduces the CSM as the long-term owner of the account, with the OBM being a temporary part of the process. The expectation for scheduling the kickoff call is somewhat based on the customer, but we need to make sure we follow up with the customer until we have something on the calendar. If the customer has deferred their start, then there will be a Chatter Notification one week before they indicated they would like to get started to remind you to reach out. 4. 🔧 Installation & Setup Customers receive a learning assignment email directed to their technical contact and any partner contact listed. This walks them through the installation and configuration of Blackthorn apps in Salesforce. The instructions are also available in the ?My Onboarding? tab in the community. The OBM ensures that team assignments, community user setup, and installation tasks are correctly allocated. 5. 📚 Learning Hub Access Any customer, regardless of onboarding stage, can access the Learning Hub for self-paced education. They can also attend Office Hours for real-time support. These resources are available to guide them through any part of their journey. 6. 💬 Onboarding Syncs & Ongoing Support Onboarding Syncs : Throughout the process, regular syncs (check-ins) are conducted with the customer to track progress, address any concerns, and ensure everything is on track for Go-Live. These syncs are crucial touchpoints for collecting feedback and making real-time adjustments. The expectation for these syncs is that they will be scheduled either Weekly or Bi-Weekly, starting at the Kickoff call and ending at go-live. The OBM and customer communicate through Chatter or direct contact as needed to provide support and guidance throughout the journey. 7. 🔄 Go-Live & Handoff to CSM Go-Live : The Go-Live occurs after the customer?s first event to ensure everything has gone smoothly. Once this step is completed, the customer is moved out of onboarding. CSM Takeover : From this point, the CSM takes over regular check-ins and continues the relationship with the customer to ensure their ongoing success and satisfaction. 8. 🔗 Post-Onboarding & Ongoing Engagement After onboarding, the customer can continue to access the Blackthorn community , use the Learning Hub , and attend Office Hours for ongoing support. The CSM remains the primary contact, ensuring a seamless transition from onboarding to regular account management. Internal Key Takeaways: Cross-team Collaboration : The onboarding journey involves close coordination between the Sales , CSM , and Onboarding teams, with the OBM playing a temporary role during onboarding. The CSM can be a pivotal and truly helpful advocate to keep pushing customers to keep moving forward. Tailored Onboarding : Each onboarding process is customized based on the Pre-Onboarding Survey and continuous feedback gathered during onboarding syncs to make sure that we are addressing what the customer needs, and we are providing the resources that most benefit them. Smooth Go-Live : A successful Go-Live occurs after the customer?s first event, ensuring everything works as expected before transitioning them out of Onboarding to the CSM for ongoing support.

What is Re-Enablement? 
 Re-Enablement - We should only verbally offer a re-enablement plan when: The customer has tried office hours to a reasonable degree. (Trackable via reporting) We have already performed a tech audit or custom use case meeting to ensure the system is properly configured. Customers have been out of onboarding for over 6 months or 1 year and are struggling. The CSM has already met with an OBM internally before making the offer to the customer and they are both in agreement that a re-enablement is needed/justified. 
 If the CSM and the Onboarding team agree upon re-enablement (in the CSX Slack channel), the path followed will depend on the customer's ARR or strategic value. The path should be decided upon during the internal meeting with the OBM and CSM before making the offer.  
 Self-Guided Path (Low ARR/Strategic Value) OBM will create a COM record for the customer with a re-enablement record type. OBM and CSM will meet with the customer to offer re-enablement and show them how to access their re-enablement COM. ( Note: Health score will not move to onboarding as their re-enablement will be tracked through a COM record ) OBM and CSM will track progress of the customer?s personnel through assigned material. Customer will leverage office hours during this period for additional help. Once key personnel have completed assigned material, OBM will schedule a reverse demo with the customer and CSM. ( Note: OBM will use the CSM?s recommendations to establish who the key players are for each customer. ) Upon completion of the reverse demo, if the customer has demonstrated a good level of understanding of the Blackthorn platform, the OBM will update the COM record and it will be marked as ?Done? and the re-enablement will have ended.  
 Guided Path (High ARR/Strategic Value) OBM will create a COM record for the customer with a re-enablement record type. OBM and CSM will meet with the customer to offer re-enablement and show them how to access their re-enablement COM. ( Note: Health score will not move to onboarding as their re-enablement will be tracked through a COM record ) During this call, OBM will ask for a cadence that works for the customer to help them stand up their pressing event. Assigned OBM will meet with the customer for the cadence agreed upon.  OBM and CSM will track progress of the customer?s personnel through assigned material. Once key personnel have completed assigned material, OBM will schedule a reverse demo with the customer and CSM. ( Note: OBM will use the CSM?s recommendations to establish who the key players are for each customer. ) Once the pressing event is stood up and successful and reverse demo has been completed, COM will be marked as ?Done? and the re-enablement will have ended.

Secondarily, Identify Pain Points: Share challenges or issues faced during the event creation or management process. Are there any gaps in your events or things you WISH you could do?  1. Authorized User Credentials: Walk through the authenticated user access to ensure proper authentication. 2. Licenses: Review licensing status and ensure all necessary licenses are in place. 3. Permission Sets: Verify user permissions and ensure permission sets align with roles. Verify user permissions align with the signed contract. Blackthorn Logs: Examine logs for critical errors and other indicators of system health. 7. Custom Processes/Flows: Review custom processes and flows to ensure they do not conflict with Blackthorn?s operations. Assess for inefficiencies or potential optimizations in customizations. 8. Current Use/Use Case: Evaluate current usage of Blackthorn features to ensure they are being leveraged effectively. Paylink & DocumentLink Authorization: Check if these authorizations are functioning as intended. Post-Audit Recommendations 1. Audit Summary: Provide a comprehensive summary of findings, identifying issues, recommendations for feature optimization, and steps for improvement. 2. Ongoing Health Monitoring: Introduce a Running Account Tech Health Score that monitors product usage and system health, with annual or as-needed reviews to ensure continued alignment with business goals. 3. Product Upgrades and Future Features: Recommend new features or upgrades that could benefit the customer, ensuring they stay up-to-date with Blackthorn?s latest offerings. Scheduling the Audit The audit can be conducted through a live session or a recorded walkthrough. If recorded, an email summary will be provided with action items and follow-up recommendations. It is not to be confused with AppExchange apps, which are third-party applications. Instead, the apps you create in your org help organize your workflows, like Blackthorn Events, which is simply an app inside your Salesforce instance. 
 What is a Salesforce App? A Salesforce app is a customizable group of objects, tabs, and other elements centered around a particular business function. For example, when using Blackthorn, it?s treated as an app within Salesforce?everything related to events, such as attendees, tickets, or payments, is grouped together into this app for easy access. 
 Each app includes: Tabs : Visual elements that represent objects or functionalities. For instance, tabs might include accounts, contacts, or specific event records. Objects : Tables in Salesforce that store data. Custom objects might be created for specific purposes, like managing event sessions or attendees. Components : Visual elements or pieces of functionality, such as dashboards, forms, or automations. Apps make navigation in Salesforce more intuitive. Content: Content Name: What is a Lookup Relationship in Salesforce
Content Introduction Text:
Introduction In Salesforce, a Lookup Relationship is a way to loosely link to objects together so they can share data. In other words you are saying "These two records are related but don't depend on each other to exist". 
 How does a Lookup Relationship work? A Lookup Relationship has a few key items to understand: 
 Relationship: With a Lookup, the relationship doesn't have a strict dependency. For example if you relate a Contact to an Account the Contact can still exist independently of the Account being changed or deleted. Navigation: These allow you to easily navigate between related records. You can click on a Contact's related Account and you'll be navigated directly to the Account record. Shared Fields: The Lookup relationship allows you to share fields between the objects. This is especially helpful in reporting and when setting up Blackthorn Email Templates.
Content Conclusion Text:
FAQs Question: What if I delete a record with a value in a Lookup field? Answer: This would be allowed but keep in mind the child records (records looking up to this one) would be "orphaned" so if you deleted an Attendee in Blackthorn, their invoice would still exist for example. 
 
 
 Conclusion In summary, lookup relationships provide a flexible way to connect records between objects without making them strictly dependent, allowing Salesforce users to build connections across data without needing rigid dependencies.

Content Introduction Text:
Introduction Security basics include controlling data access to ensure your users can view, edit and interact with what they need while less relevant or protected data is hidden. This is controlled by a few key concepts: 
 Profiles Baseline Access : Every user in Salesforce has a profile. This defines their baseline permissions like what objects they can access, what actions they can preform (Create, Read, Edit, Delete) as well as access to specific fields Page Layout and Apps : Profiles also control which page layout and app your users can see. this helps streamline your interface for your role. Permission Sets Extending Access: Permission sets allow you to grant additional permissions to users without changing their profile. For example, if you need temporary access to an object for a special project you're working on or new object that is created a permission set can be used to grant this without creating a new profile. Flexibility: Unlike profiles, multiple permission sets can be assigned to one user. This allows for flexibility for managing permissions across teams. They can also have an expiration date when assigned to help with permission management. 
 Together Profiles and Permission Sets are the foundation for what your user can do within Salesforce. Your visibility of, ability to edit and delete any object or field value are controlled by these. 
 How does Record Sharing work? Record sharing is another layer of security in a Salesforce org. When we say record sharing we mean your access to a particular piece of data. For example your profile may give you access to view and edit an Account but depending on record sharing you may not be able to view or edit certain accounts that are owned by another team in your organization. Record sharing using roles in a hierarchy for access to specific records. 
 Role Hierarchy: The role hierarchy determines data visibility on a record level based on users roles within the organization. Users higher in the role hierarchy (such as managers) can see records owned by users lower in the hierarchy. Sharing Settings: The role hierarchy works together with org-wide sharing settings to define who can see what records. The Blackthorn objects for example are set to Public Read/Write meaning all users can view/edit any records of these objects by default.
Content Conclusion Text:
FAQs Question: Why can't I delete a Blackthorn record if it is set to Public read/write? Answer: The ability to delete records is not granted by the Public read/write. This is controlled by the user's permissions as well as the role hierarchy. Note many Blackthorn records will be created/owned by the authorizing user of the events app. 
 
 
 Conclusion In summary, Salesforce security includes combining profiles and permission sets for object level and field-level access with the role hierarchy for record level sharing. This is fairly complex but lets your Salesforce Admin create a flexible security model that meets your organization and individual needs.

Content Introduction Text:
How do I add SMS Messaging to Custom Objects? 
 What Is Adding SMS Messaging to Custom Objects? With Blackthorn Messaging, you can extend SMS communication capabilities to any custom object in Salesforce. This feature allows you to send and track SMS messages from records in your custom objects, such as leads, service cases, or any business-specific data you?re managing. By integrating SMS messaging into your custom objects, you can streamline communications, enhance engagement, and keep all messaging records centralized within Salesforce. Benefits of Adding SMS Messaging to Custom Objects Enhanced Communication : Engage customers, leads, and contacts directly through SMS from any custom object, improving response times and enhancing the overall user experience. Centralized Record Management : Keep track of SMS history directly within the related record, allowing for a complete view of all customer interactions. Compliance Controls : Easily manage opt-outs and messaging preferences through fields like  Do Not SMS , ensuring communication remains compliant with regulations. Customizable Integration : Tailor the SMS experience by linking SMS records to specific custom objects, creating targeted messaging flows that align with your business processes. Steps to Add SMS Messaging to Custom Objects Create a Lookup Relationship Link the  SMS Message Object  to your custom object by creating a lookup field, enabling the association of SMS messages with your custom records. Example : If you?re adding SMS messaging to a custom  Attendee  object, create a lookup relationship on the  SMS Message Object  to tie it to individual attendee records. Add a 'Do Not SMS' Field Create a checkbox field on your custom object to help manage consent and preferences for SMS communications. This ensures that you comply with customer communication preferences and opt-out requirements. Create a Phone Field Add a  Phone  field to your custom object to specify which number SMS messages should be sent to. Example : Label it as "SMS Phone" to distinguish it from other phone fields. Update Page Layouts and Related Lists Make sure the  Do Not SMS  and  SMS Phone  fields are visible on the page layout of your custom object. Add a related list for  SMS Messages  to display all SMS interactions associated with each record. Add the Blackthorn Messaging Component to Lightning Pages Integrate the  Blackthorn Messaging Messenger  component into the Lightning page for your custom object, enabling users to send and receive messages seamlessly from the record page. Configure Permissions Assign appropriate permission sets, like  Blackthorn Messaging Standard User , to ensure that users can access and interact with SMS features. Verify that users have necessary access to the  SMS Message Object  and related fields. Example Use Cases Event Follow-Up : Imagine you have a custom object for  Event Attendees . By adding SMS messaging, you can send event reminders, updates, or follow-ups directly from the attendee record. Customer Support Cases : Add SMS messaging to a custom  Support Case  object to send quick updates to customers, ensuring prompt and clear communication.
Content Conclusion Text:
FAQs Question:  Why do I have to add the  Attendees  object if it?s already a Blackthorn object? Answer:  Not all customers use the Blackthorn Events app, so the  Attendees  object is not included as a standard connection for messaging. This ensures flexibility, as not every customer has the  Attendees  object in their Salesforce org. By allowing you to add it manually, we ensure messaging can be tailored to fit your unique needs. 
 Question:  How do I ensure that contacts do not receive unwanted SMS messages? Answer:  Use the  Do Not SMS  field to control messaging preferences and prevent messages from being sent to specific records. Additional Resources Blackthorn Documentation on Custom Object Configuration

Creating Events with the Event Builder: Cloning Events & Using Event Templates

 There are multiple ways to create an event: ? Begin from Scratch ? Build an event manually, field by field. ? Clone an Event ? Copy an existing event and make adjustments. ? Edit an Existing Event ? Modify an event already in your system. 
 Cloning is a great option when you have similar events and want to save time by reusing an existing setup rather than starting from scratch. In this guide, we?ll cover: 
 🔹 How to access the Event Builder 🔹 How to clone an existing event 🔹 Using Event Templates for efficient event creation 📍 Accessing the Event Builder The Event Builder is available in two places: 1?? From an Event Record ? Use the "Event Builder" button to edit the event you?re currently viewing. 2?? From the Blackthorn Events Apps ?  Let?s focus on Cloning an Event and how to use Event Templates to make your workflow more efficient. 
 🔄 What Does "Clone an Event" Do? Cloning an event copies all of the details from a parent event into the Event Builder. This means:

 💡 Think of it like duplicating a Google Doc ?you get an exact copy, but you can tweak it before saving. 
 How to Clone an Event in the Event Builder: 1?? Open the Event Builder (via the tab). 2?? Choose "Clone an Event" from the options. 3?? A list of past events will appear? select the event you want to clone . 4?? The Event Builder will load the cloned event with all details pre-filled . 5?? Review and modify the details as needed. 6?? Click Save ?this creates a new event record based on the clone. 
 📌 Important Notes: Registrations do not carry over from the parent event. If using ticketing, review pricing to ensure it?s still accurate. Always double-check event-specific details like dates, venues, and descriptions. 
 Event Templates: The Smarter Way to Clone What?s the Difference Between Cloning and Using a Template? Cloning an event copies all details from an existing event , while an Event Template is intentionally designed to be cloned. 
 💡 Templates act as pre-configured event blueprints that include standard settings, branding, and common event types so you don?t have to reconfigure them every time. 
 Why Use Event Templates? ? Standardized event formats ? Keep branding, ticket types, and event structure consistent. ? Faster event creation ? No need to set up core details from scratch. ? Eliminates repetitive work ? Set event types (like ?Webinar? or ?In-Person Conference?) once and reuse them. 
 🛠? How to Set Up an Event Template for Cloning 1?? Create a New Event Record Go to Blackthorn Events and click New Event . Name it something recognizable (e.g., "Webinar Template" or "Annual Gala Template"). 2?? Configure All Core Settings Set up the event type (Virtual, Hybrid, In-Person). Add standard ticket types, pricing, and registration settings . Customize branding, descriptions, and automation rules. 3?? Mark the Event as a Template (Optional) Use a custom field or add "Template" to the event name to distinguish it. 4?? Save the Event ? This event now serves as a reusable template for cloning. 
 📌 Next Time You Need a Similar Event: Instead of creating a new event from scratch, simply choose "Clone an Event" and select your template! 
 ? Final Check ? When to Clone vs. When to Use a Template Scenario Clone an Event Use an Event Template You want to duplicate a past event with minimal changes. ? Yes ? No You need a reusable format for different event types. ? No ? Yes You want to copy specific settings from an event. ? Yes ? No You need all branding, ticketing, and formatting pre-set. ? No ? Yes You frequently host similar events (e.g., monthly webinars). ? No ? Yes
