Content: Content Name: Event Builder: In-Person, Virtual, & Hybrid Events
Content Introduction Text:
Event Builder Walkthrough: Setting Up Event Types in Blackthorn When setting up an event in Blackthorn , the first step is choosing an Event Type . This determines whether your event will be: 
 ? Virtual (Online only) ? In-Person (Venue) (Attendees meet at a physical location) ? Hybrid (A combination of both virtual and in-person attendance) 
 Your selection affects which fields appear in the Event Builder. 
 📍 Step 1: Selecting an Event Type 1?? Open the Event Builder (from the tab in your navigation bar). 2?? Under General Information , locate the Location Type section. 3?? Choose one of the following options: Virtual ? If the event is online-only. Venue ? If the event is at a physical location. Hybrid ? If the event has both in-person and virtual options. ? The Event Builder will automatically update to show the relevant fields based on your selection. 
 🖥? Setting Up a Virtual Event When you select Virtual , a Webcast Account section appears, allowing you to connect your event to an online meeting platform. 
 📍 In the Event Builder ? Webcast Account Section Webinar/Meeting Account ? Choose a linked Zoom, GoToWebinar, or WebEx account to automatically create the meeting/webinar in both Salesforce and your online meeting platform upon creation of your event. You'll learn how to do this later. Paste Webinar/Meeting URL ? Alternatively, you can just paste in a link to an already created webinar/meeting into the webinar/meeting field. 
 🏢 Setting Up an In-Person (Venue) Event When you select Venue , a Venue Account section appears to enter physical location details. 
 📍 In the Event Builder ? Venue Section Venue Account ? Search for a pre-existing venue in your Salesforce environment. Venue Name ? Enter the name of the location. Address Details ? Fill out the street, city, state, and country fields. 
 📌 Pro Tip: If you frequently use the same location, create an Account for the venue in Salesforce to quickly select it for future events. The mailing address on the account is what is being referenced. 
 🌍  Setting Up Hybrid Events When setting up a Hybrid Event in Blackthorn, it's important to ensure that: 
 ? In-person attendees have a clear venue location and a QR code for check-in. ? Virtual attendees can easily access their sessions with a "Join Stream" button. ? Both groups have a smooth registration and attendance experience. 
 To achieve this, always select "Hybrid" as the event type and then configure virtual attendance using sessions . 
 📍 Step 1: Selecting "Hybrid" as the Event Type 1?? Open the Event Builder ( from the tab in your navigation bar ). 2?? Under General Information , locate the Location Type section. 3?? Select "Hybrid" 4?? Fill-out the information, venue, and webinar/meeting information needed. 
 🏢 Step 2: Setting Up the Venue (For In-Person Attendees) 📍 In the Event Builder ? Venue Section Venue Account ? Select a pre-existing venue or type in the address manually. Venue Name & Address ? Ensure attendees have a clear location. City, State, and Country ? Required for accurate location tracking. 📍 In the Event Builder ? Webcast Account Section Paste Webinar/Meeting URL ? Paste in a link into the webinar/meeting field. We will be removing this link after we save this event, so no need for it to be a real link. 
 📌 How Attendees Check In When attendees register, their AttendeeLink will include a QR code . At the event, they can scan their QR code at check-in for a seamless entry process. ? 
 🌍 Step 3: Adding Virtual Sessions (For Online Attendees) To add a virtual component to the event, create sessions with a Webinar Account or Meeting Link instead of using the Webcast Account at the event level. 
 📍 In the Event Builder ? Sessions Section 1?? Click "Add Session" and enter session details. 2?? Set a Session Name (e.g., "Keynote Speaker: Future of Higher Ed"). 3?? Choose a Virtual Meeting Option: Select a Webinar Account (Zoom, GoToWebinar, WebEx). OR manually enter a meeting link . 4?? Set Session Time & Date (must be within event start and end time). 5?? Click Save to finalize the session. 
 6?? When creating your tickets, under the Event Items section, link your sessions to the appropriate ticket so that these sessions appear during registration. 
 7?? Once the event is saved and you are taken to the event record page, find the Webinar/Meeting URL field and remove the link we added earlier. This will allow the QR code to appear for the in-person registrants. 
 
 📌 How Virtual Attendees Join Sessions If an attendee registers for the virtual session, a "Join Stream" button will appear on their AttendeeLink when the session is live. (10 minutes before the start time) ? 
 Finalizing Your Event Setup Once your Event Type is configured, review the following sections: ?? The Fundamentals ? Set your event description, dates, and time zone. ?? Event Details ? Assign categories, keywords, and visibility settings. ?? Organizer Details ? Identify the person or department responsible for the event. 
 Click Next to continue building your event! 🚀

Managing Paid Events in Blackthorn If your event requires ticket sales, registration fees, or donations,  Blackthorn Events has built-in support for handling payments ?all within Salesforce. 
 Paid Events  allows you to securely collect payments during event registration by integrating with  payment gateways  like Stripe, Authorize.net, and Spreedly. With Blackthorn, your financial data (PCI Compliant) lives  inside Salesforce , making it easy to track payments, issue refunds, and generate invoices?all without needing an external payment system. How Do Paid Events Work? When you enable payments on an event, Blackthorn connects to a  payment gateway  to process transactions. Here?s how it all comes together: 1??  A Payment Gateway (like Stripe) is Connected  ? This allows Blackthorn to process payments directly within Salesforce. 2??  Attendees Select & Pay for Tickets During Registration  ? The system automatically calculates applicable fees, taxes, and discounts. 3??  Payments Are Logged in Salesforce  ? Each transaction is recorded and tied to the attendee?s registration. 4??  Receipts, Invoices, and Refunds Are Managed in Blackthorn  ? No need to switch to another platform! 
 💡  Pro Tip:  Blackthorn integrates natively with Salesforce, so all event payments can be reported using  Salesforce Reports & Dashboards , giving you  real-time financial insights  on your event revenue. Paid Events Features in Blackthorn 🔗 Connecting a Payment Gateway To accept payments, you?ll need to  connect a payment gateway  within Salesforce. Supported options include: Stripe Authorize.net Spreedly 💰 Event Payment Features Blackthorn provides  a full suite of tools  to manage financial transactions for events. ??  Refunds  ? Process refunds directly in Salesforce (capabilities depend on your gateway). ??  Payouts & Reconciliation  ? Track payouts and match them to your event revenue for clear financial reporting. ??  Event Fees & Taxes (GST/VAT)  ? Automatically apply taxes, service fees, and additional charges. ??  Discount Codes  ? Offer promo codes and track redemptions. ??  Invoices & Receipts (DocumentLink)  ? Generate professional invoices and send receipts directly from Salesforce. ??  Write-Offs & Allocations  ? Manage event-related financial adjustments and revenue allocation. 
 
 
 Things to Keep in Mind (Limitations & Considerations) 🌍 Multi-Currency Support Blackthorn supports  multiple currencies , but some  payment gateways may have limitations  on which currencies they can process. Always check your  gateway?s documentation  to confirm currency compatibility. Blackthorn does not currently support Multi-Currency checkout for events, so you will need to select ONE currency for each event. 🏦 Payment Gateway Limitations Some features (like refunds or installment payments)  depend on the payment gateway you choose . Some notable examples are below Auth.net requires separate gateways to handle multiple currencies The Spreedly Gateway does not support Webhooks, so the Salesforce records can not be updated to reflect the status of the transaction on the Gateway. The Blackthorn/Spreedly integration does not support ACH payment natively (as a result of not supporting Webhooks) The DocumentLink feature can not be used in conjunction with the Spreedly Gateway Each gateway has  different rules for processing payouts , transaction fees, and refund timelines. Wrap-Up: Key Takeaways ?? Paid Events in Blackthorn allow you to  collect payments natively in Salesforce . ?? You?ll need a  connected payment gateway  to process transactions. 
 Now that you understand the basics, you?re ready to  configure your first Paid Event!  🎉

🎟?  Discount Codes: Giving Your Attendees the Best Deal Discount codes are a great way to  boost registrations, reward loyal attendees, or track promotions  for your event. Whether you're offering a VIP discount or a partner promotion, Blackthorn Events makes it easy to set up and apply discount codes seamlessly. 
 Let?s walk through  how to create, configure, and use discount codes  so you can offer flexible pricing options while keeping everything organized. 🔢 Types of Codes in Blackthorn When you create a code, you?ll choose a  Type . Here?s what each one does: Code Type Behavior Common Use Case Discount Applies a flat or percentage-based discount at checkout Early bird pricing, general promos, partner offers Access-Promo Requires a valid code to complete checkout for specific Event Items Internal-only or invite-only tickets Source Tracks registration activity tied to marketing campaigns (no other effect) Attribution via newsletters, partner channels 
 
 📌 Code Type is selected when you create a Code record in Salesforce. The fields that display will adjust based on your selection. 
 🛠?  Creating a Discount Code To set up a discount code, we?ll first create the code itself, then decide which events or tickets it applies to. 📍  To create a new discount code: 1?? Open the  App Launcher  in Salesforce and search for  Codes . 2?? Click  New  to create a new discount code. 3?? Fill in the details: Code Name  (e.g., ?DEALER2025?) Valid From / Valid Through  (Set start and end dates) Quantity Made Available  (How many times the code can be used?leave blank for unlimited) Type:   Select  Discount ,  Access-Promo , or  Source Discount Amount or Percentage  (e.g., $10 off or 15% off) Description  (Optional, but helpful for internal tracking!) 4?? Click  Save  to create your discount code. 
 🎯  Pro Tip:  If you don?t set a usage limit, your code can be used an unlimited number of times! Great for general promotions, but if you're offering an exclusive discount, make sure to cap it. 🔗  Assigning a Discount Code to an Event or Ticket Now that your discount code is created, we need to  tell Blackthorn where it applies ?to an entire event, or just specific tickets. 📍  To link a discount code to an event or ticket: 1?? Open the  Code Record  you just created. 2?? Scroll down to the  Code Eligibilities  section and click  New . 3?? Choose: Event  ? Code applies to all Event Items (tickets). Event Item  ? Code applies only to selected ticket(s). 4?? Click  Save  to finalize the assignment. 
 💡  Remember:  A discount code can apply to either an  Event  or an  Event Item , but not both at the same time! ??  Controlling How Discount Codes Are Used By default, discount codes are  optional  at checkout, but you can change this based on your event?s needs. 
 📍  To update how discount codes work for your event: 1?? Go to your  Event Record  in Salesforce. 2?? Find the  Code Settings  field. 3?? Choose one of the following options: Optional  (Attendees can enter a discount code, but don?t have to) Required  (Attendees  must  enter a valid code to proceed) Hide  (Removes the code field entirely from checkout) 4?? Click  Save  to apply your settings. 
 ??  Heads Up:  If you set  Code Settings  to ?Required,? every registrant  must  enter a valid discount code, or they won?t be able to check out. Make sure this is the right choice for your event! 📊  Tracking Discount Code Usage Want to see how your discount codes are performing? You can track their usage right inside Salesforce! 📍  To monitor discount codes: 1?? Open the  Code Record  in Salesforce. 2?? Check the  Quantity Claimed  field?this updates automatically every time someone applies the code at checkout. 3?? If an invoice is voided, the system will  release  the code back into available usage, so you don?t have to track it manually. 
 🎯  Pro Tip:  Use discount code tracking to measure the success of your promotions?did the DEALER25 code drive more registrations? Did your VIP promo bring in the right attendees? Use this data to optimize future discounts! 🔍 Overview: How Each Code Type Works 💸  Discount Codes What they do : Apply a flat or percentage discount to the event item price during checkout. How they work : Can be applied manually by the attendee in checkout. Discount amount is reflected in the order total. Usage is tracked via the  Quantity Claimed  field on the Code record. When to use : Promotions, early bird pricing, partner offers. 🔐  Access-Promo Codes What they do : Restrict  checkout  for specific Event Items unless a valid code is entered. How they work : The ticket remains  visible and selectable  on the event page. If added to the cart, checkout will be  blocked  unless the Access-Promo code is entered. Users must remove the restricted item or provide the code to proceed. When to use : Internal tickets, pre-release access, member-only items. ?? This restricts  checkout , not visibility. The ticket is always visible. 📈  Source Codes What they do : Track the use of a specific code for marketing attribution or internal reporting. How they work : No impact on pricing or checkout behavior. Useful for identifying how attendees arrived (e.g., which campaign or partner sent them). Usage is tracked just like any other code (via  Quantity Claimed ). 
 💡  Pro Tip: Use UTM Parameters for Campaign Tracking If you're using  Source codes  to track marketing efforts, consider using  UTM parameters  instead. They don't require attendee input and work across platforms like email, ads, and social. Learn how to implement UTM tracking in Blackthorn here: 👉  UTM Tracking in Blackthorn ??  What You Need to Know About Discount Codes 💡  Only one discount code can be used per transaction. 💡  Discount codes are not currently supported for session pricing.  They apply only to event tickets. 🔜  What?s Next? Now that you know how to  create, apply, and track discount codes , let?s move on to  Refunds ?because sometimes, plans change, and it?s good to be prepared! 💸

Content Introduction Text:
Setting Up a Paid Event in Blackthorn Events By now, you've already explored how to build out your event using the  Event Builder ?creating your landing page, adding speakers and sponsors, and structuring your sessions. Now, let?s take it one step further and turn this event into a  paid event  by assigning prices to tickets and sessions. 
 Step 1: Selecting a Payment Gateway To process payments for this event, you'll need to connect a  Payment Gateway . Navigate to the  Tickets  tab in the  Event Builder . At the top of the page, locate the  Payment Gateway  field. Select the gateway you want to use for this event. 🛠?  Pro Tip:  If your event is free, you can skip this step. No payment gateway is required for free events. Once your gateway is set, let?s move on to pricing your tickets and sessions. 
 Step 2: Setting Ticket Prices In the  New Ticket  window, you?ll see a field labeled  Price  and a checkbox for  Free . By default, Blackthorn marks tickets as free, but unchecking that box allows you to enter a price for the ticket. 
 
 💡  Reminder:  If you offer multiple ticket types, each one can have its own pricing structure. 
 Step 3: Assigning Prices to Sessions Some events include optional paid sessions that attendees can select during registration. To set a price for a session: Scroll down in the  New Ticket  window. Under  Sessions , you?ll see the list of sessions associated with this ticket. Next to each session, you?ll find a  Price  field?enter the amount you?d like to charge for that session. 💡  Reminder:  Attendees who purchase this ticket will see these session prices during checkout and can choose whether or not to add them. Next Steps Once your ticket and session prices are set, that?s it! You?ve successfully set up a paid event in Blackthorn. In the next section, we?ll cover how to configure  fees, discounts, and tax settings  to fine-tune your event checkout experience. 🚀

Content Introduction Text:
Finalizing Your Paid Event: Selecting Allowed Payment Methods 💳 🎉  You?re almost there!  You?ve set up your event, added ticket prices, and assigned session fees?now let?s make sure your attendees can actually pay for their tickets! 
 Once you?ve  saved and published  your event, it?s time to head over to your  Event Record  in Salesforce and set up your  payment methods . 🛠 Step 1: Choosing How Attendees Can Pay 💡  Blackthorn Events lets you decide which payment options to offer attendees at checkout. 
 1??  On your Event Record , find and click on your assigned  Event Settings ?? . 2?? Locate the  Enabled Payment Methods 💰  field. 3?? Click  Edit ?? , then choose from the available options: 💳 Card  ? Credit/Debit card payments ? Pay Later  ? Invoice or delayed payment options 🏦 ACH  ? Direct bank transfers (only available for some gateways) 🚀 Stripe Checkout  ? Redirects to Stripe?s hosted payment experience 4?? Click  Save ? , and you're all set! 
 ? 
 🔔  Why does this matter?  Giving attendees multiple payment options makes checkout smoother and increases completed registrations! 
 💡  Pro Tip:  Every Blackthorn-supported gateway allows for  Card 💳  and  Pay Later ?  payments at a minimum. Additional options like  ACH 🏦  or  Stripe Checkout 🚀  depend on your specific gateway configuration. 🔜 What?s Next? Now that we?ve made sure payments are enabled, let?s talk about  fees, taxes, and GST ?because nobody likes surprise costs at checkout. 💰 
 👉  Next up: Configuring Fees & Taxes for Your Event

💰 Taxes & Fees: Fine-Tuning Your Event Checkout Now that we?ve got our event set up, pricing configured, and payment methods selected, it?s time to talk about  fees and taxes ?the often-overlooked details that can make a big difference in your event finances! Whether you're charging attendees a  processing fee  or ensuring compliance with  sales tax/GST , Blackthorn Events makes it easy to set up these charges seamlessly. 
 Let?s dive into  where these fees come into play, how they function, and how to set them up  in your event! 🚀 🎯  What Are Fees in Blackthorn Events? In Blackthorn Events,  fees  are additional charges applied at checkout to account for costs like  payment processing  and  sales tax . These are completely configurable and ensure that you?re covering necessary expenses without surprising your attendees. 
 You can add two types of fees to an event: 1??  Payment Processing Fees 💳  - Helps recover the cost of transaction processing. 2??  Tax Fees 🏦  - Automatically applies taxes based on your event?s location or tax requirements. Each of these fees can be  customized, assigned to an event, and automatically calculated  at checkout to ensure smooth and transparent pricing for your attendees. 🏗  How Fees Work in Blackthorn Events When an attendee registers for a paid event, Blackthorn Events determines: ??  If a Payment Processing Fee applies  ? Based on their selected payment method (e.g., credit card vs. ACH). ??  If tax needs to be calculated  ? Based on how the event organizer has configured sales tax settings. These fees are then  automatically added to the attendee?s final checkout total  before they complete payment. Pretty handy, right? 😉 🛠  Configuring Fees for Your Event Now, let?s set up fees for our event! 🎟 1??  Creating a New Fee Navigate to  Fees  in Salesforce. Click  New  and enter the details: Fee Name  (e.g., ?Credit Card Processing Fee? or ?Sales Tax 10%?) Fee Percentage  (e.g., 2.9% for processing fees or 10% for taxes) Type  (Payment Processing or Tax) Tax Display Setting  (optional) Save the record! 2??  Assigning the Fee to Your Event Open your  Event Record  in Salesforce. Locate the  Tax Fee  or  Payment Processing Fee  field. Select the appropriate Fee record from the list. Save the event! ? Once configured, these fees will  automatically be applied at checkout  based on your event?s setup?no manual calculations needed! 🎉 📌  Understanding How Fees Appear at Checkout Depending on your settings, your attendees may see: 💵  Processing Fees:  Added to their final total (but only if they use a card for payment!). 🛒  Taxes:  Either included in the ticket price or added at checkout as a separate line item. If you choose to show tax as a separate charge, attendees will see a  breakdown of their total cost  before finalizing payment, making the pricing transparent and clear. ??  A Few Things to Keep in Mind? Processing fees apply only to card transactions  (not ACH payments). Taxes can be displayed in two ways  ? included in the ticket price or added at checkout. Once a fee is assigned to an event,  it applies to all purchases, UNLESS the Event Item (Or Donation) is marked as "Tax-Exempt." Want to double-check your setup? You can always test your fees by  registering for your own event and going through the checkout process  to see how the charges apply! 🕵???? 🎉  Wrapping Up By configuring your  Payment Processing Fees and Tax Fees , you ensure a  smooth and transparent checkout experience  while also covering important costs behind the scenes. Blackthorn Events gives you the flexibility to apply the fees you need?without overwhelming your attendees with unexpected charges. 
 👉  Next up:  We?ll look at  Discount Codes ?because your Attendees love to feel special!

📄  DocumentLink: Delivering Invoices & Receipts with Ease Now that we?ve covered  refunds , let?s talk about another important part of event payments? making sure attendees get the right documentation for their purchase . Whether they need a  receipt for their records  or a  formal invoice to pay from or for accounting ,  DocumentLink  makes it simple to send attendees the paperwork they need. 
 After all, once an attendee registers and pays for an event, they may expect an  instant confirmation or a way to access their payment details later . Instead of handling this manually, Blackthorn Events  automates the entire process ?making your life easier while keeping things professional for your attendees. 
 One of the coolest features is that if your Attendee has Opted to "Pay Later" the DccumentLink works as both an invoice AND a way for them to pay using the "Pay" button on the screen! 
 Let?s walk through how it works! 🚀 💡  What Is DocumentLink? DocumentLink is a  fully customizable invoice and receipt generator  inside Blackthorn. It automatically creates a  personalized document for each transaction ?whether it?s an  invoice for an unpaid balance  or a  receipt for a completed payment . 
 This means that every attendee can quickly and easily access their financial records without you needing to manually send anything. 🎉 🛠?  How DocumentLink Works for Event Checkout Here?s what happens behind the scenes when an attendee registers for a paid event: 1??  An Invoice is Created  ? When someone registers for an event and completes payment, an  Invoice record  is automatically generated in Salesforce. 2??  DocumentLink Generates an Invoice or Receipt  ? If your event has a  DocumentLink Template  assigned, the system will create a branded invoice or receipt using your predefined layout. 3??  Attendees Get Their Document  ? A  DocumentLink URL  is generated, allowing attendees to  view, download, or print their invoice or receipt  at any time. This link can be included in  confirmation emails  or accessed later if needed. 💡  No more manual invoice requests?everything is handled automatically! ??  Setting Up DocumentLink for Your Event 📍  To ensure your attendees get a branded, personalized version of their invoices or receipts, follow these steps: 1?? Create a DocumentLink Template Open the  App Launcher  and search for  DocumentLink Templates . Click  New  and fill in: Template Name  (e.g., "Standard Event Receipt") Terms & Conditions URL  (if applicable) Acceptance Language  (for credit card or ACH payments) Company Logo & Contact Info  (adds branding to your invoices!) Save  your template. 🎨  Pro Tip:  You can customize your DocumentLink Template with additional fields like  invoice numbers, event details, and disclaimers  to match your business needs. 
 2?? Create a flow to assign the Template to Your Invoices We recommend a short flow that fires when an invoice record is created and updates the DocumentLink Template field with the DocumentLink Template you just created! Here's a resource that will show you how to set this up! 🎯  Now, every attendee payment will automatically generate a professional, branded invoice or receipt. 🔍  How Attendees Access Their Invoice or Receipt Once the event checkout process is complete, attendees can  access their payment details  in several ways: ?  Via Confirmation Emails  ? The DocumentLink can be included in the  registration confirmation email , giving attendees instant access to their receipt. ?  Through the Event Portal  ? If you?re using  Experience Cloud , attendees can retrieve their invoices on demand. ?  Manually via Salesforce  ? If someone requests an invoice, you can always find the  DocumentLink URL  on their  Invoice Record  and send it to them directly. 
 💡  Want to make sure invoices go out automatically?  You can set up  Salesforce automation  (using Flow or Process Builder) to send DocumentLink invoices the moment an invoice is created! ??  Heads-Up: A Few Things to Keep in Mind 📜  Invoices vs. Receipts:  DocumentLink generates  invoices for unpaid balances  and  receipts for completed payments ?so you'll be good to go no matter what! 🌍  Multilingual Support:  You can set the  Display Language  field on the template to ensure attendees receive documents in their preferred language. 📩  Customization:  Want to add legal disclaimers or specific refund policies? Use  custom fields  on your DocumentLink Template to include all necessary info! 🔜  What?s Next? Now that we?ve covered  how to process payments, refunds, and invoices , let?s talk about  Write-Offs & Allocations ?because sometimes, payments need adjustments, and it?s important to know how to manage financial records properly.

💰  Payouts: Tracking Your Event Revenue Like a Pro Your event was a hit! 🎉 Tickets were sold, payments were collected, and now it?s time for the most important part? getting the money into your bank account. While  you  might not need to check Payouts often, your  finance or accounting team definitely will.  They?re the ones who: 👀  Verify deposits  to ensure event sales match funds received. 📊  Reconcile payments  in accounting systems. 💰  Monitor cash flow  to keep everything running smoothly. 
 So even if you don?t personally track payouts, knowing  where to find them in Blackthorn  will make you a hero when finance comes knocking! 🚀 🔍  How Do Payouts Work? When an attendee pays for a ticket, the funds  don?t immediately  land in your bank account. Instead, they go through your  payment gateway  (Stripe is currently the only Payment gave away that suppor), which then deposits the money on a schedule?usually  daily, weekly, or monthly . ?  The Stripe Gateways Handle Payouts Automatically  ? No need to manually request deposits! 💡  Finance teams rely on payout data to reconcile transactions , so knowing how to track them in Blackthorn is key! 📍  Where to Find Payout Records in Blackthorn To check  when and how much money was deposited  into your bank: 1??  Go to the Transactions Tab in Salesforce. 2??  Filter by "Transaction Type = Payout." 3??  Review the details, including: Payout Amount 💰  ? The total funds deposited. Date 📆  ? When the deposit was sent to your bank. Fees & Adjustments 📊  ? Any deductions from the payment gateway. Related Transactions - easily reference any and all transaction records related to this payout record. 💡  Pro Tip:  Your finance team can cross-check this data with  bank statements  or  payment gateway dashboards  to ensure everything matches up! 🔄  Automating Payout Balance Updates Blackthorn  automatically updates payout balances  so you don?t have to track them manually. 🕒  Every day, the system runs a balance update job: ?  Updates Stripe Balance & Salesforce Balance fields  (so your records always match what?s available and pending). ?  Pulls in new Payouts & Adjustments  (so you stay up to date). 💡  This means your payout data stays accurate and finance always knows what?s coming in!  🚀 🚀  Best Practices for Payouts ?  Regularly check payout records  to ensure your sales match the funds deposited. ?  Communicate with finance  so they know where to find payout details in Blackthorn. ?  Use balance updates  to keep your Salesforce records in sync with your payment gateway. 🔜  What?s Next? 🎉  You made it!  We?ve now covered every major piece of  Paid Events in Blackthorn ?from collecting payments to processing refunds, sending invoices, and tracking revenue. How else can Blackthorn make things easy for you?

How do I add attendees to my event? Adding Attendees ?on the back end? means you (an internal user) put people into an event  without  making them fill out the public form themselves. Blackthorn gives you a few supported paths that still trigger all the right automations (invoices, emails, attendee links, etc.). Use these instead of hand?building Attendee records. 
 You?ll mainly pick between: Registering  as them  on the public page Using the  Attendee Registration Lightning Component , Bulk-loading people into the  Attendees tab / Event Builder  as ?To Invite.? Each has trade?offs around ticket types, payment, and data collection.
Content Conclusion Text:
Use Cases I?m an Event Coordinator  who just got a phone call: ?Register me now.? I have their info, it?s one ticket ? I use the  Lightning Component  from the Contact record. I?m a Marketer  prepping a VIP list: I want to invite 500 alumni to self-register ? I bulk-add from a Campaign in the  Attendees tab , then hit  Send Invite . I?m a Support/Admin  fixing one missed registration: I need the full automation (sessions, payment) ? I register them on the  public event page  and choose  Pay Later  if needed. I?m an Event Builder  setting everything up at once ? While building the event, I drop attendees in via the  Event Builder Attendees tab  to send invites later. Sub-Features 
 Attendee Registration Lightning Component 🔷 Fast, in-Salesforce registration for a single ticket type. Benefits / Use cases: Register someone instantly from their Contact/Lead/Account/Event record. Data pre-fills; no need to ask basic questions again. Limits:  One ticket type per batch, no session selection UI, payment usually handled via Pay Later/invoice. Attendees Tab (Event Record) 📋 Bulk add lists as  To Invite , then auto-email the link. Benefits / Use cases: Pull from Accounts, Campaigns, Reports, or other Events (up to 2,000). Curate before sending?status starts as  To Invite ;  Send Invite  flips to  Invited  + emails. Watch out:  If you actually need them  Registered  right away, this isn?t it. Make sure report column 1 is the Record ID or the import fails silently. Event Builder ? Attendees Tab 🧱 Do the same bulk ?To Invite? add while configuring the event. Benefits / Use cases: Keeps everything in one workflow during build. Great for preloading your invite list. ?Send Invite? Automation ?? Updates statuses and fires emails. Benefits / Use cases: One click to notify everyone sitting in ?To Invite.? Consistent messaging using your template. ?New Attendee? Button (Inside the Tool) ? The  only  recommended ?manual entry? because it still triggers downstream logic. Use case:  One-off add when you don?t have them anywhere else. FAQ?s Question:  Can I mix different ticket types for people in one go with the Lightning Component? Answer:  No. Everyone in that registration batch gets the same ticket type. Do separate submissions or use the public page. 
 Question:  Why don?t I see session selection in the Lightning Component? Answer:  Sessions are selected by the attendee later via their attendee link. 
 Question:  My report isn?t working in the Attendees tab tool?what?s wrong? Answer:  The report type must be Contact/Account/Lead/Attendee/Campaign Member  and  the Record ID must be the first column. (Docs: https://docs.blackthorn.io/docs/bt-events-attendee-builder) 
 Question:  What?s the max I can add at once from the Attendees tab? Answer:  2,000 records per add action. Break larger lists into chunks. 
 Question:  Why shouldn?t I just create an Attendee record manually (field by field)? Answer:  You?ll skip auto-related records (invoices, attendee links, etc.) and break reporting. Use supported methods. 
 Question:  Does ?Send Invite? immediately email people? Answer:  Yes? IF the provided workflow/flow is active . Verify the template first. Content: Content Name: Managing Departmental Access to Events in a Shared Salesforce Org
Content Introduction Text:
Keeping Department Events Separate in a Shared Salesforce Org 
 When multiple departments use Blackthorn Events in the same Salesforce org, things can get messy fast. Suddenly, event planners from one department can see or even edit events from another. Confusion sets in. Data gets mixed. And no one?s sure whose event is whose. If this sounds familiar ? you?re not alone. It?s a common challenge for universities, nonprofits, and large organizations running cross-departmental event programs. 
 The good news? You can solve it with a few smart Salesforce configurations. 
 1. Use Record Types to Keep Departments Organized Record types are your best friend here. Assign each department its own record type, and you can tailor page layouts, picklists, and defaults to their specific needs. That means your ?Admissions? team and your ?Advancement? team can both plan events ? without stepping on each other?s toes. 
 Bonus: Record type selection now works right inside Blackthorn?s Event Builder! 
 Why it works: Record types make it obvious which department an event belongs to and naturally separate views, automation, and layouts. 
 2. Add a Validation Rule for an Extra Layer of Safety Even the best configurations can?t stop every click. That?s where a validation rule comes in. You can set a rule so that an event can?t be saved or updated unless the user?s department matches the event?s department. 
 Why it works: If someone accidentally lands on another department?s event, Salesforce gently stops them before any changes stick. 
 3. Apply Sharing Rules to Control Who Sees What Use criteria-based sharing rules to make sure each department only has edit access to their own events. 
 Why it works: Sharing rules handle the behind-the-scenes visibility, so users see only what they need to ? keeping data clean and private without creating a dozen custom profiles. 
 4. Make It Clear When Users Are ?Out of Bounds? A little visual feedback goes a long way. Try filtered list views or Lightning page filters that only show events from the user?s department ? or even display a banner when someone views another department?s record. 
 Why it works: It?s a friendly, visual reminder that they?ve wandered outside their team?s events. 
 The Bottom Line By combining record types, sharing rules, and validation rules, you can keep every department focused on their own events while still operating smoothly under one org. 
 It?s a simple setup that prevents confusion, protects data, and gives every event planner the confidence that they?re working in the right place.

Content Introduction Text:
Understanding Matching and Duplicate Rules for Event Attendees 
 When someone registers for an event, Salesforce needs to decide whether to use an existing Attendee record or create a new one. That?s what the Matching Rule and Duplicate Rule control. 
 The Goal You want to avoid duplicate Attendee records , especially when: Someone was directly invited through their AttendeeLink , but instead registers through the public registration link . You also want attendees to be able to register for different events that share the same name (like ?Annual Training? held every year). 
 How It Works 1. BT Events Attendee Matching Rule This rule looks for an existing Attendee before creating a new one. It uses Event ID , not Event Name, to tell events apart (important if you have multiple events with the same name). If it finds a match, it updates that same Attendee record instead of creating a new one. If it?s disabled , Salesforce will always create a new Attendee record ? duplicates will happen. 2. BT Event Attendee Duplicate Rule This rule decides whether Salesforce should allow duplicates at all. ?Allow? (default) ? Always creates a new Attendee record (duplicates allowed). ?Block? ? Checks for an existing Attendee using the Matching Rule. If one is found ? Salesforce uses that existing record . If someone tries to register again with the same name and email ? They?ll see this message: ?Warning: Duplicate email registration not allowed.? What You Should Do Since you don?t want duplicate Attendee records , you should: Enable both the BT Events Attendee Matching Rule and the BT Event Attendee Duplicate Rule. In the Duplicate Rule settings, set Action on Create = ?Block.? Make sure your Matching Rule is the new version that uses Event_ID instead of Event Name. This ensures that attendees can register for multiple events with the same name without creating duplicates within a single event. 
 Example Scenario Let?s say you invite John Doe to an event with his personal AttendeeLink ? but he ignores that and instead registers through the public registration page. With Matching + Duplicate Rules enabled (?Block?) Salesforce will find John?s existing Attendee record (same event, same email) and update it , not create a new one. ? Without Matching + Duplicate Rules, or if set to ?Allow? Salesforce won?t check for duplicates ? it will create a new Attendee record , causing confusion and extra cleanup. ? 
 How This Differs from Relationship Settings Relationship Settings control how the system connects your Attendee records to Contacts, Leads, or Accounts in Salesforce ? basically, it manages who the attendee is related to. The Matching and Duplicate Rules , on the other hand, control whether a new Attendee record is created or an existing one is reused for the same event . 
 Here?s the difference: 
 Feature What It Controls Example Matching & Duplicate Rules Whether Salesforce reuses or creates an Attendee record when someone registers Prevents multiple ?John Doe? Attendees for the same event Relationship Settings Which Salesforce record (Contact, Lead, or Account) the Attendee is linked to Decides if ?John Doe? the Attendee connects to an existing Contact or a new one 
 So in short: Matching/Duplicate Rules ? Stop duplicate Attendees for the same event. Relationship Settings ? Decide who that Attendee is related to in your CRM (Contact, Lead, etc.). They work together , but they solve different problems . 
 Setup Steps Summary Go to Setup ? Duplicate Rules. Click BT Event Attendee Duplicate Rule ? Edit. Set Action on Create = ?Block.? Under Matching Rule , select BT Events Attendee Matching Rule (Event_ID version). Save your changes. 
 Bottom Line Setting What Happens Recommended? Matching Rule OFF + Duplicate Rule = Allow Always creates new Attendees ? No Matching Rule ON + Duplicate Rule = Allow Still creates duplicates ? No Matching Rule ON + Duplicate Rule = Block Updates existing Attendees (no duplicates) ? Yes
